reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.szoveg: I am looking for a system for a family home This is the most common situation: the house is there, the size of the household is known, and the question is which solution belongs here. Four things decide the choice — the plot, the load, what becomes of the treated water, and the permitting conditions. We work through them in order. Choosing

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.szoveg: Choosing a solution type The order is not arbitrary: the plot's characteristics narrow the field, and choosing a technology only makes sense within it. 01 The disposal of the treated water comes first. If there is nowhere for the treated water to go, choosing a unit is pointless. Infiltration into the ground, a surface receiving water or reuse — at least one of them has to work. 02 Then the technology. For permanent occupation the biological unit is the most common choice, because it works in a smaller area and to a better outlet quality. The septic tank comes into play where there is enough room for the soakaway field on well-draining soil. 03 Capacity comes last. Sizing is done for the design load, not the average — the stated occupancy and the expected peak give it together. 04 And at every step, the permitting conditions. These differ by municipality and can override a solution that is otherwise technically sound. Plot

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.szoveg: Plot suitability At an existing house part of the plot is already built on, so where the free area lies is a constraint too. Four things are worth looking at. 01 Free, accessible surface. Installing the unit needs machinery, and later sludge removal a tanker. If the chosen position cannot be reached, that makes operation more expensive for decades. 02 Soil and groundwater. The permeability and the design groundwater level decide the method of disposal and the area required. 03 Protective distances. Dug and drilled wells — yours and the neighbours' — plot boundaries and buildings together fix the usable band. 04 The route and depth of the existing connection. This decides whether the connection can be made by gravity or needs a pumping station too. Sizing

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.szoveg: Capacity and occupancy Capacity follows not from the floor area of the house but from the actual load. Sizing is based on the size of the household and the specific water consumption, together with the expected fluctuation. It is worth thinking ahead: if the family may grow, or guests come regularly, that has to be allowed for in the sizing. Extending later is considerably more expensive than one size up at the outset. A substantially over-sized system is no advantage either: the biological process adjusts to the actual load, and a persistently low load affects the efficiency. The aim is not the largest unit but the one that fits the design load. Cost

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.szoveg: Cost and installation The final total is rarely driven mainly by the price of the unit. The items below are worth reckoning with, because they account for the difference between two apparently identical projects. 01 Earthworks. The size of the excavation, how cohesive the soil is and where the spoil goes — on rocky or very cohesive ground this is a significant item. 02 The depth and length of the connection. A deep connection may need a pumping station, which means both capital and running cost. 03 Disposal of the treated water. Building the soakaway field or the run to the receiving water — a different order of magnitude depending on soil type and distance. 04 Electrical connection. The unit needs power; if it sits far from the distribution board, the cabling is a cost too. 05 Permitting and documentation. Its extent depends on the solution type and the local requirements. 06 Operation. Electricity consumption, periodic sludge removal and maintenance — without these the solutions cannot be compared. Next step

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.cim: When are you ready to request a quote?
reszek.szoveg: When are you ready to request a quote? When you know the size of the household, roughly how much free area the plot has, and you have some idea where the treated water could go. That is already enough to ask for a sensible quote — the survey settles the rest. From a few questions, the decision aid shows which solution type is in play and what cost range to reckon with. The result is indicative. Or request an on-site survey Fill in the decision aid Frequently asked questions

reszek.lap: I am looking for a system for a family home
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often How much room does the unit take up in the garden? The unit itself goes below ground, with only the chamber covers visible at the surface, so the garden stays usable. The area required is determined not by the tank but by the disposal of the treated water — with a soakaway field that is a considerably larger surface. Can the system be heard, or does it smell? In normal operation, no. The compressor that provides the aeration is quiet and is typically housed in a protected position. Odour is always a signal: it points to a blockage, sludge removal left undone or a fault, so a service engineer should be called. What is its electricity consumption? It comes from the continuously running compressor, and depends on the size of the unit. The specific value is in the data sheet of the chosen model; we give it in the quote together with the expected annual running cost.

Assessing an existing system Here something is already in the ground — known only in part, or not at all. The purpose of the survey is to record the starting condition: what is known, what is uncertain, and what has to be looked at on site. Why this differs from new build

reszek.cim: Something is already in the ground
reszek.szoveg: Something is already in the ground Replacing a cesspit is not the same project as a system installed at a new house. Here there is already an underground system known only in part, or not at all, existing pipework and an established use of the plot — and every one of these affects the construction. So the purpose of the survey is not only to design the new system but to recording the starting condition: what is known, what is uncertain, and what has to be looked at on site. Preparation

reszek.cim: What you can gather — and what you should not judge
reszek.szoveg: What you can gather — and what you should not judge What you can prepare photographs of the cover, its surroundings and the access; earlier documents, if any exist; the emptying history — how often and who carries it out; the symptoms observed: odour, overflow, backing up; a simple site sketch — where the structure and the house are; the estimated year of installation, if you know it. What you should NOT have to judge the structural condition — cracking, settlement, ageing; watertightness — that is a matter for testing; environmental compliance; whether any element can be retained in the new arrangement; the inside of the tank — opening old chambers is dangerous; do not climb in and do not lean over it. On site

What we look at 01 The existing structure its type, material, estimated size, position and accessibility. 02 The level of the pipe coming from the house. This determines the depth at which the new unit is set, and whether a riser or a pumping station is needed. 03 The area available for the new tank and for disposing of the treated water. 04 The soil and the visible water conditions. 05 Access for installation and for later servicing. 06 How the changeover runs — how the property stays usable during the work. What becomes of the old system

reszek.cim: We do not promise that anything can be reused
reszek.szoveg: We do not promise that anything can be reused Sometimes part of the existing pipework, or the structure itself, can be kept in another role — but this only once the actual condition is known can be decided. Until we have seen it, we do not promise it. Decommissioning the old structure is part of the project and a cost item: the method of emptying, backfilling or demolition can be a permitting question too. Next step

reszek.cim: Let us put together what you have
reszek.szoveg: Let us put together what you have The project brief gathers the data on the existing system, the plot and the use — from which the technical direction and the factors driving the cost can be determined. Or request a survey Cost and project brief
Biological system or septic tank? „Holiday home = septic tank” is too simple. The critical variable is the length and recurrence of the gaps — not seasonality itself. Not a rule but a condition

reszek.cim: „Holiday home = septic tank” is too simple
reszek.szoveg: „Holiday home = septic tank” is too simple We recommend the EPURECO septic tank system specifically for intermittently used properties, because it is passive and needs no continuous power. That does not, however, make it an automatic rule: the area the drainage field needs, the soil and the groundwater decide just as much. An active biological system, on the other hand, cannot be ruled out merely because the property is not continuously occupied — the critical variable is the the length and recurrence of the gaps, not seasonality itself. Directions

What tips it which way It tips towards the septic tank if… the breaks are long and recurrent — a few times a year, with gaps of months; there is no power during the absence, or it is shut down for the winter; the soil is well draining, and there is room for the drainage field; as little operating duty as possible is what you want. It tips towards active biological treatment if… use is regular during the season — weekly, for instance; the free area is limited, the drainage field would not fit; the soil is cohesive or the groundwater is high; permanent occupation in the longer term is also on your mind. Operation

reszek.cim: What the two directions ask for differently
reszek.szoveg: What the two directions ask for differently 01 Power. The active system requires a continuous supply; the septic tank does not. 02 Sludge handling. Both have some, but in a different rhythm and a different way. 03 Additive. In the A.B. Clear system the bacterial culture is fed by the incoming wastewater. With EPURECO, after a longer break the manufacturer recommends a refreshing additive — this is an operating requirement, not a general biological rule. 04 Checks during an absence. At a seasonal property it matters whether someone looks in on the system from time to time. What we still have to pin down

reszek.cim: We give no specific duration here
reszek.szoveg: We give no specific duration here The A.B. Clear controller includes holiday mode for a planned absence. Exactly how long a gap it is meant for, however, we will publish only on approved technical data — until then we say so at the survey, for your own pattern of use. Next step

reszek.cim: What happens during the long break?
reszek.szoveg: What happens during the long break? Operation during absence and the conditions for taking it back into use raise most of the questions here — worth seeing clearly before you buy. Or look at the seasonal cases Long absences and restarting

Building a usage profile „Holiday home, 4 people” is too little to decide on. The annual pattern of use becomes a load profile — and from that it emerges which directions remain relevant. What it is for

„Holiday home, 4 people” is too little This tool does not choose a product. From the annual pattern of use it builds a load profile from which it can be decided which technological directions remain relevant — and what plot or technical data is still missing. „I do not know” is acceptable on every question, and each question says whether it affects the technology or only the sizing. What it asks

Four groups 01 Calendar of use. Which months, how often, for how long — and how long the longest gap is. 02 Occupancy. Typical and maximum, and how often the maximum occurs. 03 Load. Water consumption where known; washing machine, dishwasher; guest peak; letting. 04 Conditions during absence. Whether power stays on, whether the building is winterised, whether anyone looks in from time to time. The module

The profile builder The profile builder is not live yet. Its rules — which answer closes or opens which direction — cannot be written until the gap thresholds are approved. This is the same open question this hub marks throughout. Until then, describe your pattern of use in a few sentences and we will go through it with you: Get in touch. In the meantime

reszek.cim: Let us talk about how you use it
reszek.szoveg: Let us talk about how you use it Write and tell us which months and how often the property is used, and how long the longest break is — that is already enough for us to say which direction is in play. Get in touch

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.szoveg: I am about to buy a plot or build This is the point where most can be gained — and most lost. The conditions for wastewater treatment are encoded in the plot: settle them before buying or designing and the solution can be built into the plans. Discovered afterwards, the correction always costs more. Suitability

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.szoveg: Could the plot be suitable? Five factors decide what can be built. None of them is visible in the listing, but every one can be found out before purchase. 01 Soil structure. The permeability determines whether the treated water can be soaked away at all, and if so over how large an area. On cohesive clay soil infiltration either does not work or works only with a considerable area. 02 Groundwater level. A high or widely fluctuating groundwater level bears on two things: whether the unit can be sited and whether infiltration is possible. What has to be looked at is the seasonal maximum, not the current value. 03 Disposal of the treated water. Infiltration into the ground, a surface receiving water or reuse — if none of these is available, the range of solutions narrows to the sealed holding tank. 04 Protective distances. Dug and drilled wells, water base protection zones, plot boundaries and buildings: together these fix where the unit and the soakaway field can go. 05 Access. Installation needs machinery, and later sludge removal a tanker. If the unit's position cannot be reached, that makes operation more expensive for decades. Soil investigation

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.szoveg: Soil, groundwater and water disposal The soil and the groundwater are not a technical detail but the project's most important input. Permeability and the design groundwater level together decide whether the treated water can be disposed of within the plot, and if so over how large an area. Before purchase this needs no full geotechnical report: the experience of neighbouring properties, the data sheets of nearby drilled wells and whether water stands on the plot in spring say a great deal. Accurate sizing, however, will require measurement before the works begin. If a geotechnical report is being prepared for the build anyway, ask the expert to include the wastewater aspects — one investigation then answers two questions. Documents

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.szoveg: What documents may be needed? The exact list differs by municipality and by solution type. Those below are the ones that come up in most projects — worth reckoning with at the design stage. 01 Title deed and map extract. The legal position of the plot, its encumbrances and exact boundaries — necessary in its own right before purchase. 02 The relevant part of the local building regulations. Buildability, utility provision requirements and any local restrictions. 03 Geotechnical report. Usually prepared for the build; what sizing the wastewater treatment needs from it is the permeability and the groundwater level. 04 Water permit documentation. Whether it is required, and in what depth, depends on the solution type and the local requirements. We can say precisely after the survey. 05 The unit's declaration of performance. Part of the manufacturer's documentation; it may be asked for at permitting and at handover alike. Checklist

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.szoveg: Plot data checklist before buying Knowing the answers to these before the purchase decision leaves no room for surprises. Every one can be answered by viewing the plot, asking at the council and talking to the neighbours. 01 Is there a mains sewer in front of the plot, and if not, is one planned? Ask for a schedule, not verbal information. 02 What is the soil like, and does water stand on the plot in spring? Water standing for long periods points to a high groundwater level or poor permeability. 03 Where are the surrounding dug and drilled wells? Their protective distances narrow the buildable area. 04 Is there a surface receiving water nearby? A ditch, a stream or a channel — and who manages it. 05 Does the plot lie in a water base protection or other protected area? This overrides every other consideration, so it is worth starting here. 06 Can the back of the plot be reached by machine? Both the installation and later sludge removal require it. Next step

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.cim: An on-site survey before the decision
reszek.szoveg: An on-site survey before the decision If the plot is a candidate but some of the questions above are unanswered, an on-site survey is the quickest route. At the survey we look at where the installation could go, how the water would be disposed of, and the access — that is, exactly what the price and the feasibility follow from. Worth doing before purchase too: if the plot turns out to be unsuitable, it is better to know before the contract. Or look at which solutions are in play Request a survey Frequently asked questions

reszek.lap: I am about to buy a plot or build
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Can you carry out a survey before purchase? Yes. With the owner's consent the plot's characteristics can be examined before the purchase. This is the most common request from people buying in an area without a sewer who would rather not meet the constraints afterwards. How much more expensive is it if we only look at wastewater after the house is designed? The difference is not caused by the price of the unit but by the workarounds: a longer pipe run, a deeper connection, fitting a pumping station, or an awkwardly placed soakaway field. Together these add up to a significant item, and they are hard to put right afterwards. What should I do if the soil is unsuitable for infiltration? Another means of disposing of the treated water then has to be examined: a surface receiving water or reuse. If neither is possible, the sealed holding tank remains — we will say so even when our system does not follow from it.
Campsites and community facilities Long periods of low occupancy, then full capacity within a short time. Design needs not the maximum but the seasonal curve.

reszek.cim: The most extreme load of all
reszek.szoveg: The most extreme load of all At campsites and in community systems the load often varies far more sharply than at a permanently occupied property: long periods of low occupancy, then full capacity within a short time. So design needs not the maximum headcount but the seasonal occupancy curve, the daily peaks, the number of sanitary blocks, any catering — and whether the wastewater arrives from several buildings or from a shared collection system. What you need to provide

The seasonal and community profile 01 The type of facility. Campsite, holiday camp, community accommodation, a cluster of houses, a shared system for several properties, a small part of a settlement. 02 Maximum and average occupancy. The gap between the two is at its widest here. 03 Monthly or seasonal occupancy. Broken down by month — this is the single most important set of figures. 04 Peak days. Long weekends, holidays, events. 05 The number and position of the sanitary blocks. Several connection points call for a different network arrangement. 06 Restaurant, kitchen, mosoda. Separate water streams. 07 Condition out of season. Fully closed, minimal security staff, or partial operation. 08 The layout of the internal drainage network. With several buildings this is a design task in its own right. Shared operation

reszek.cim: What is not a technical question
reszek.szoveg: What is not a technical question With a community system — a cluster of houses, a shared solution for several properties, part of a settlement — ownership and operating responsibility is a substantive question in itself, and the long-term success of the project typically turns on it. To be settled in advance: who keeps the log, who carries out the regular checks, who calls the service engineer, and how the operating cost is shared. For a programme-based installation the regulations also set requirements for a responsible service provider and for monitoring — so a community project cannot be treated as several family homes added together. Two seasonal risks

reszek.cim: What has to be handled separately
reszek.szoveg: What has to be handled separately A long period of low load The biology is left without nutrient An active system needs a separate operating mode or a shutdown Closing the season is a planned process The power supply is a question during the break too A passive system tolerates this better A sudden returning peak The first weekend of the season is often a full house straight away The biology takes time to restart The opening of the season has to be scheduled in advance This is an operating task; it does not happen by itself The sizing has to withstand the returning peak as well Next step

reszek.cim: The form of the system is a question too
reszek.szoveg: The form of the system is a question too With several buildings, several connection points and a need for expansion, a modular arrangement comes into play. The overview page in the Solutions section works through this. Technical project brief Larger and community systems Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Does it have to be sized for the maximum capacity? Not necessarily — but the seasonal peak cannot be ignored. The right approach starts from the seasonal curve: how long the peak lasts, how often, and what average sits beneath it. The wastewater comes from several buildings. The layout of the internal collection network is then a design task in its own right, and the form of the system is a question too: one central plant or several distributed units. This is one of the project's early decisions. Who is responsible with a shared system? That is for the owners to decide, and it is worth recording in writing: who operates it, who keeps the documentation, and how the cost is shared. Many community projects stall not on technical grounds but at exactly this point. We do not operate in winter. What should happen to the system? That calls for a planned closing and opening procedure. The exact steps depend on the technology — and that is precisely why seasonality is an input to the choice of technology, not an afterthought.

Capacity and occupancy Capacity does not follow straight from the number of occupants. Under-sizing and over-sizing are both risks, and a guest peak is not necessarily a basis for sizing. The common misunderstanding

reszek.cim: „Four of us live here, so we need a four-person unit”
reszek.szoveg: „Four of us live here, so we need a four-person unit” Capacity does not follow straight from the number of occupants. Sizing is done for the the design load , which the actual water consumption, the intensity of use and the expected change give together. So four things have to be handled separately: the number of permanent residents , the people regularly present , the occasional guest peak, and the lasting growth expected in future. Two mistakes

reszek.cim: Under-sizing and over-sizing are both risks
reszek.szoveg: Under-sizing and over-sizing are both risks If it is persistently under-sized the system cannot maintain its treatment efficiency; the load places greater demands on the unit as well; extending later is considerably more expensivethan one size up at the outset. If it is needlessly over-sized the biological process adjusts to the actual load; a persistently low load affects the efficiency too; the investment and the space required grow needlessly. Guest peak

reszek.cim: The Christmas gathering is not necessarily a basis for sizing
reszek.szoveg: The Christmas gathering is not necessarily a basis for sizing A few days of guest load do not necessarily justify a larger unit chosen for the maximum momentary occupancy. The systems take a short period of excess load — the extent and the duration, however, have to be stated model by model, not as a general rule. For your own case we say at the sizing stage how much peak the configuration in question will take. Data source

reszek.cim: Measurable at an existing house, to be estimated on a new build
reszek.szoveg: Measurable at an existing house, to be estimated on a new build 01 On an existing house the annual or monthly consumption on the water bill is a far better basis than the nominal headcount — it is an actual figure. 02 On a new build there is no consumption history: the composition of the household, the intended use and the expected growth have to be recorded in a structured way. 03 Working from home is not headcountbut intensity of use — daytime presence increases consumption. 04 The result is a range, not a model. The final configuration comes from an approved sizing, with expert review in borderline cases. Next step

reszek.cim: What does the whole project consist of?
reszek.szoveg: What does the whole project consist of? The price of the unit is rarely the largest item. The next page works through what else belongs to it, and who takes on what. Cost and installation

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.szoveg: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system? Behind the everyday word „cesspit” stand three solutions that the law also treats separately. The choice starts not from price but from whose conditions your property can meet. Terms

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.cim: Three operating models, not three products
reszek.szoveg: Three operating models, not three products Behind the everyday word „cesspit” stand three solutions that the law also treats separately: the sealed holding tank collects and has the contents removed periodically; the a septic tank system pre-treats without any energy input, and most of the treatment happens in the drainage field; the active biological treatment unit genuinely cleans the water in an aerated process. The choice starts not from the price of the unit but from whose conditions your property can meet — and which operating duty you are willing to take on. What has to be weighed

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.cim: Eight criteria, for all three solutions
reszek.szoveg: Eight criteria, for all three solutions 01 Use. Permanent or intermittent — this is the strongest filter. 02 Power supply. The active system requires continuous power; the other two do not. 03 Plot and soil. The drainage field of a septic tank system calls for a considerable area and adequate permeability. 04 Groundwater. It affects both the installation and the water disposal. 05 What becomes of the treated water. If it has nowhere to go, the range of solutions narrows to the sealed holding tank. 06 Whether emptying is acceptable. With a sealed holding tank this is part of how it works, not a fault. 07 Maintenance you can take on. In an active system the compressor and the membrane are wearing parts. 08 Points of failure. Only the active system has moving parts. When it is NOT the right choice

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.cim: Every solution has a situation where it is not right
reszek.szoveg: Every solution has a situation where it is not right 01 The sealed holding tank is not right where use is intensive and the frequency or the arranging of emptying is untenable. 02 The septic tank system is not right if there is not enough area for the drainage field, the soil is cohesive or the groundwater is high. 03 The active biological system is not right where there is no continuous power, or the property is used only a few times a year with long breaks. What we have to prove

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.cim: We back the limits of application with our own data
reszek.szoveg: We back the limits of application with our own data In this market the limits of application are communicated differently by different manufacturers — one recommends the same technology for seasonal use, another for permanent. So we have to support our own rules with our own project data, not with a competitor's claim or a marketing one. Next step

reszek.lap: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.cim: The total cost, not the price of the unit
reszek.szoveg: The total cost, not the price of the unit The economics of replacement are not a comparison of the emptying charge with the purchase price of the unit. The next page shows what else belongs to it — and why we make no „pays for itself in X years” promise. Or let us look at what is in the ground now Total cost and payback
Choosing a solution type With permanent occupation, active biological treatment is the natural starting point — but not an automatic conclusion. The plot can override it. The starting point

reszek.cim: Permanent occupation is not yet enough to decide
reszek.szoveg: Permanent occupation is not yet enough to decide For a permanently occupied family home, active biological treatment is the natural starting point — but not an automatic conclusion. The space the plot allows, the soil, the groundwater, the power supply, the disposal of the treated water and the operating duty you can take on may override it together. The order of the choice: the disposal of the treated water first, then the technology, and capacity last. The other way round, you find out mid-project that it cannot be built. What the user actually notices

Five differences 01 Whether power is needed. Continuously with the active system; not with the passive ones. 02 How much hely is what is needed. The larger item is not the tank but the disposal of the treated water — with a septic tank, the drainage field. 03 What routine duties there are. With an active system, checks and wearing parts; with a passive one, less, but not nothing. 04 How the sludge is handled. With a sealed holding tank the whole volume is taken away; with the other two, sludge is handled periodically. 05 Where the water goes. This decides which direction is in play at all. When it is not right

reszek.cim: All three solutions have such a case
reszek.szoveg: All three solutions have such a case 01 The sealed holding tank is not right where, with permanent occupation, the frequency or the arranging of emptying is untenable. 02 The septic tank system is not right if there is not enough area for the drainage field, the soil is cohesive or the groundwater is high. 03 The active biological system is not right where there is no continuous power, or the property is used with long breaks. Next step

reszek.cim: Can it be sited on the plot?
reszek.szoveg: Can it be sited on the plot? The technology only becomes relevant if the plot allows it. The pipe level, the groundwater and the water disposal together decide what can be built. Or the question of capacity Plot suitability
Cost and installation The project is not the same as the unit. Cost structure, boundaries of responsibility — and what stays with the owner even with the sludge bag system. Reframing the question

„What does a treatment unit cost?” There is no single number for this, because the project is not the same as the unit. The plot's characteristics and the scope of service you ask for bring further elements with them — and these are often larger items than the tank itself. So here we show cost structure is what we show, not a price: which items to look for in the quote, and which plot figure the exact total still depends on. Cost structure

reszek.cim: What the project is made of
reszek.szoveg: What the project is made of 01 Unit and delivery. 02 Earthworks and lowering into place. Driven by how cohesive the soil is and where the excavated earth goes. 03 Pipework and electrical preparation. 04 A riser or a pumping station, where the pipe level requires it. 05 Disposal of the treated water. A soakaway field or the run to the receiving water — a different order of magnitude depending on soil type and distance. 06 Commissioning and documentation. 07 Dealing with the old system, if there is one on the plot. 08 Operation. Electricity, maintenance, wearing parts — without these two quotes cannot be compared. Liability

Who carries out what What you can ask of us delivering and lowering the unit into place; installation and making the connections; commissioning and handover; the technical documentation; the service backing afterwards. What your own contractor can also do the earthworks; the electrical preparation; preparing the site for the day of delivery; in that case the boundaries of responsibility have to be settled in advance — this is the most common source of dispute afterwards. Operation

What stays with the owner With the sludge bag technology there is no regular emptying — that is a real advantage. It does not, however, make it a system with nothing to do, and it is better to know that before buying than after. What remains: handling the sludge bag and composting the surplus sludge, the regular checks, the membrane and the compressor as wearing parts, and checking the ventilation. In an exceptional situation — after a sustained overload or a fault, for instance — outside intervention may also be needed. Next step

reszek.szoveg: You are ready to request a quote? What makes a project ready for a quote is not reading the content but the data. The next page checks that. Readiness to request a quote

Type, estimated age and size, material, position, emptying frequency, problems observed, accessibility. 02 The use. Could the plot be suitable? The tank almost always fits somewhere. The system, however, only works if the treated water also has somewhere to go and the connection can be made. This is a pre-screening, not a technical approval. The real question

reszek.cim: It is not whether the tank fits
reszek.szoveg: It is not whether the tank fits The suitability of a plot is not a question of geometry. The tank almost always fits somewhere — the system, however, only works if the the treated water also has somewhere to go, and the connection can be made by gravity or with a pumping station. So the examination looks together at the mains sewer position, the expected load, the relative positions of the house and the system, the pipe level, the free area, the soil, the groundwater and the final disposal of the water. On an address and a plot size no one can issue a verdict of „suitable” — ours included. This is a pre-screening, not a technical approval. States

Three outcomes are possible The pre-screening does not give a yes or no but tells you how much uncertainty is left — and what to do about it. 01 Standard situation. The data is known and shows no risk. The project can go on along the usual route. 02 Further data is needed. One or more critical figures are missing — typically the groundwater, the soil or the depth of the pipe exit. This is the most common outcome, and it is not bad news. 03 An expert survey is needed. The plot is not technically standard: a deep pipe exit, little free area, uncertain water disposal or contradictory data. Here the site decides, not the paperwork. Risk

reszek.cim: What changes the design — and what rules it out
reszek.szoveg: What changes the design — and what rules it out It changes the design but does not rule it out high or fluctuating groundwater — a different installation method comes into play; a deep wastewater pipe exit — a pumping station can solve it; cohesive, poorly draining soil — it overrides the method of water disposal; a steep slope — it affects where the system sits and the levels; restricted access — installation and later servicing cost more. It may rule out an on-site solution the treated water has nowhere to go — no infiltration, no receiving water, no reuse; the mains sewer is technically available, and the capacity is there too; a water base protection or highly sensitive area, where separate conditions apply to the installation; there is not enough free area for either the system or the disposal of the water. Legal framework

What the regulations name explicitly For the sizing and construction of a standalone treatment facility, the regulations expressly name the characteristics of the soil, the depth of the subsurface water and the quantity of wastewater. These are therefore not technical details but decision factors the regulations themselves recognise. In a sensitive area or one with high groundwater, further conditions may apply. The classification of the area and the local requirements always have to be established with the competent authority. Next step

Understand what affects what Soil, groundwater and water disposal are interrelated — and most misunderstandings arise from treating whether the tank can be installed and whether the water can be disposed of as one question. They are two separate decisions. Or gather the plot data Soil, groundwater and water disposal

reszek.lap: I am looking for a solution for a business or institution
reszek.cim: „How many people?” is particularly misleading here
reszek.szoveg: „How many people?” is particularly misleading here For business or institutional wastewater, „how many people use it?” is not enough information to size on. The daily volume of water, the peak load, how occupancy varies over time, and the wastewater itself origin matters at least as much. A twenty-bed guesthouse, a three-hundred-pupil school and a plant employing fifty may all give the same number — and produce three entirely different projects. So this page does not recommend a product as its first step. Its purpose is to categorise it: whether it can be treated as a standard domestic-type load, or whether it calls for bespoke engineering, pre-treatment, laboratory work, permitting and operational planning. The first separation

reszek.cim: What is the origin of the wastewater?
reszek.szoveg: What is the origin of the wastewater? Domestic in character Bathroom, WC, handbasin, washing Its composition resembles household wastewater The load is proportional to the number of users Conventional biological treatment can be applied Laboratory analysis is typically not a precondition Most accommodation, offices and schools belong here Process or commercial kitchen Arising from a production process or a production kitchen Its composition depends on the activity It cannot be derived from headcount It may require pre-treatment Laboratory analysis is typically unavoidable Industry-specific discharge requirements may apply Which kind of facility?

Guesthouses and accommodation Bed count is not load. Occupancy, peak weekends, season, laundry, spa — and operation out of season. Guesthouse, accommodation→ Restaurants and commercial kitchens Kitchen wastewater cannot be treated like that of a dwelling with the same headcount. Pre-treatment and laboratory data. Restaurant, kitchen→ Schools and institutions A strong daily rhythm, a drop at weekends, long holidays — and an organisational question over who the responsible operator will be. School, institution→ Campsites and community facilities Wildly varying load, several points of use and shared operating responsibility. Campsite, community→ Plants and special loads „Plant” is not a sizing category. Separating the domestic and process water streams, laboratory data. Plant, industrial→ Technical project brief A structured data package from which it can be decided whether a standard configuration or engineering design follows. reszek.lap: I am looking for a solution for a business or institution
reszek.szoveg: Seven questions, in order Together these answers establish whether this is a standard or a bespoke project. 01 What is the facility, and what is the origin of the wastewater? This is the single most important question — everything else follows from it. 02 What is the actual load? Average daily volume of water, peak, seasonality. At an existing facility the water bill is the best starting point. 03 Is there any special water use? A kitchen, a laundry, a spa, process washing — each is a separate water stream. 04 Which capacity category does it fall into? The legal boundary is 50 PE — above it a different design and permitting route follows. 05 Where does the treated water go? Into the ground, to a surface receiving water, or for reuse — all three are separate routes. 06 Who will be the responsible operator? On a business project this is an organisational question, not only a technical one. 07 What expansion is expected? If the facility grows, that has to be allowed for now.

reszek.lap: I am looking for a solution for a business or institution
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is it enough if I say how many of us work there? Fine as an entry figure, but not sufficient. For a business or institutional load, headcount is particularly misleading: what counts is how much water is used, when, and whether the wastewater is domestic in character. At an existing facility the water bill is the best starting point. Do you treat abattoir or dairy wastewater? We handle special loads on the basis of bespoke engineering analysis. This is not automatic suitability: sampling, laboratory data and a feasibility study come first. A standard plant is not automatically suitable for any industrial wastewater — we say so in advance. How long until I get a quote? It depends on the data available. For a purely domestic load with known water consumption, quickly. For process wastewater, laboratory analysis and a feasibility study come first — there the first step is sampling, not the quote. Is a permit required? On a business or institutional project typically yes, and the procedure depends on the capacity, the origin of the wastewater and the receiving water. The permitting questions are covered in detail on the larger-systems page in the Solutions section.
Guesthouses and accommodation A twenty-bed guesthouse is not the same load open all year as one that fills only on summer weekends.

Bed count is not load A twenty-bed guesthouse is not the same load situation running continuously at 70–80% occupancy as one that fills only on summer weekends. To determine the load, besides the bed count you need the actual or intended occupancy rate, the months of opening, the length of the peak season, the short periods of full occupancy, and where possible the actual water consumption figures. What you need to provide

The accommodation load profile 01 Bed count and average annual occupancy. The two together give a realistic average. 02 Peak occupancy. When it is full, for how long, and how many times a year. 03 Months of opening. Open all year or seasonally. This affects the choice of technology too. 04 The difference between weekends and weekdays. For city and resort accommodation this can run in opposite directions. 05 Number of staff. They represent a load for the whole of the opening hours. 06 Catering. Breakfast only or a full restaurant. If there is a kitchen, that is a separate stream — see the restaurants page. 07 Laundry. Laundry done on site or by an outside service. An in-house laundry is a substantial, concentrated water use. 08 Wellness facilities. Pool, jacuzzi, sauna — changing the pool water is a separate, large one-off volume. 09 Actual water use. For an existing property this overrides everything — the water bill is the best figure there is. Two extremes

reszek.cim: The same number of beds, a different system
reszek.szoveg: The same number of beds, a different system All year round, evenly A predictable average load The biology receives a continuous load Less variation, less headroom needed An active biological system is typically a good choice The peak can be handled as a short overload In season only, with peaks A long period of low or zero load Full occupancy returning all at once Opening the season is an operating task in itself The choice of technology is a question too, not only the size More headroom and a different operating mode are needed Out of season

reszek.cim: What is most often left out of the design
reszek.szoveg: What is most often left out of the design At a strongly seasonal property, how the system behaves during periods of underload or complete gaps, and what operator intervention is needed at the start and end of the season, have to be examined separately. This is not a technical detail: the bacterial community of an active biological system needs a continuous supply of nutrient, and after a long break the restart takes time. The first full house at the opening of the season is not the ideal moment for the biology to be still building. That is why we ask about the out-of-season state too — not out of politeness. Next step

reszek.cim: If there is a restaurant too
reszek.szoveg: If there is a restaurant too With your own restaurant or production kitchen, the kitchen wastewater is a separate stream: with a different load and typically a need for pre-treatment. Technical project brief Restaurants and commercial kitchens Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often My guesthouse has twenty beds. Do I need a twenty-person system? Probably not. The bed count shows the maximum, but sizing starts from the average occupancy and the regular peaks. Give us the annual occupancy and the number of peak weekends — a considerably more accurate picture comes together from that. We hold events as well. An event is a short, very large peak, and it is typically not worth handling with the size of the unit — that would mean over-sizing on every other day of the year. Give us the frequency and the scale, and we will look at the right approach. We have a pool. Does that count? Filling the pool and changing the water is a large, one-off volume — it has to be flagged separately, because entering the wastewater system it can cause a hydraulic shock. In many cases it can be handled separately. We operate seasonally. Which technology is better? This is precisely the situation where the choice of technology is a question too, not only the size. Give us the months of opening and the longest break — from that it emerges whether an active system with a separate operating mode, or the passive solution, is the more relevant.

Holiday or seasonally used property Intermittent use is not „less” than permanent occupation but a different task. Biological treatment is a living process: during a long absence the system slows down, and restarting takes time. This has to be allowed for when the technology is chosen, not afterwards. Load

What does intermittent load mean? The essence of biological treatment is that micro-organisms break down the pollutants. The process presupposes a continuous supply of food: if no wastewater arrives for weeks, the activity of the biological community falls off. With seasonal use this causes two kinds of problem. First, after a long break the system does not reach full treatment efficiency straight away. Second, after the restart a large load often arrives all at once — a weekend full of guests produces considerably more wastewater than the system is prepared for at that moment. So at seasonal properties the question is not how many people use it but what the pattern of use is: a few days a week, one weekend a month, or a continuous summer period — these call for different solutions. Choosing

Biological system or septic tank? It tips towards a biological system if… use is regular — there is a load weekly or fortnightly during the season, for instance; the plot does not allow a large soakaway field, because the area is limited or the soil is cohesive; you would put the treated water to use, for irrigation during the season for instance; permanent occupation in the longer term is also on your mind — holiday homes often become permanent ones. It tips towards the septic tank if… use is infrequent and unpredictable — a few times a year, with long breaks of several months; there is no reliable power supply, or the property is shut down for the winter; the soil drains well, and there is enough free area for the soakaway field; you want as little operating duty as possible, and you accept the larger area it takes. Operation

Long absences and restarting If you choose a biological system for a seasonal property, a few operating rules will bring the efficiency back quickly. 01 The system does not have to be drained at the end of the season. The water and sludge left in the tank hold the biological community that revives when the next season starts. 02 Switching the aeration off entirely is not advisablewhere that is possible. Reduced operation gives a considerably shorter restart than a complete shutdown. 03 Give the system time after the restart. Full treatment efficiency does not return on the first day; during that period the quality of the outlet water is temporarily poorer. 04 Avoid a sudden peak load in the first days after starting up. If you can, do not schedule a large gathering for the opening of the season. 05 A check before the season is a worthwhile step. Checking the condition of the compressor, the membrane and the cover forestalls a shutdown mid-season. References

Seasonal case studies Intermittently used properties make up a substantial share of the projects so far: weekend houses, fishing lodges and holiday homes, where the load concentrates in the season. We publish the individual case studies in the Results section, after obtaining the customer's consent. Next step

reszek.cim: Start by recording the usage profile
reszek.szoveg: Start by recording the usage profile At a seasonal property the sizing starts from the pattern of use: how many times, with how many people and for how long the property is used over the year. These few figures say more than the size of the property. The decision aid takes this into account and shows which technology better suits the way you use the property. Or compare the two technologies Fill in the decision aid Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Does the system have to be drained for winter? No. The water left in the tank protects the structure and preserves the biological community that starts up again the following season. Draining does more harm: empty, the system can suffer frost damage, and the restart takes longer too. What happens if we do not use the property at all for a year? Biological activity then falls off considerably, and the restart takes longer. With a pattern of use like that it is worth examining whether the septic tank solution suits better — at the survey we can tell you specifically. Will a weekend full of guests overload the system? The units take an occasional peak load, but it has to be reckoned with when choosing. So sizing is done for the design load rather than the average — the peak has to be stated in advance, not discovered afterwards.

reszek.lap: I already have a system and need help
reszek.szoveg: What can we help with? Identifying a fault Odour, backing up, an unusual noise or a stopped compressor: the first step is to decide whether the cause is operational or technical. Faults→ Routine maintenance Checking the sludge level, inspecting the membrane and the compressor, and periodic sludge removal — these are what give the system its life. reszek.lap: I already have a system and need help
reszek.cim: What is worth checking before you call a service engineer
reszek.szoveg: What is worth checking before you call a service engineer In some cases the problem has an operational cause and can be settled with a few minutes' checking. This list does not replace a service call, but it helps describe the situation more precisely. 01 Is there power at the unit? A tripped circuit breaker or an unplugged connector is the most common reason a compressor has stopped. 02 Is the compressor running? A quiet, even sound is normal. Complete silence and unusually loud, uneven running are both signals. 03 When was the sludge last removed? Sludge removal left undone is the most common cause of falling efficiency and of odour. 04 Has the load changed? More occupants, a longer stay by guests, or several weeks away all affect how the system behaves. 05 Has anything gone into the system that does not belong there? Wet wipes, fat, paint, medication or disinfectant in large quantities all harm the biological process. Customer support

reszek.lap: I already have a system and need help
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often The unit did not come from you — can you help? In many cases yes, particularly on operating questions and for a survey. With parts the type decides: if that manufacturer's component cannot be obtained, we say so rather than recommending an unsuitable substitute. How often does the sludge have to be removed? That depends on the load and the type of unit, so it cannot be stated in general. Checking the sludge level is part of routine maintenance, and the timing of removal follows from it — planning by the calendar is not the way. What does it mean if I notice a smell near the system? Odour is always a signal, not a normal operating state. Its most common causes are sludge removal left undone, a loss of aeration, or a blocked vent. If the power supply and the compressor are in order, it is worth calling a service engineer.

reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Which situation should I start with if several fit me? With the one that comes first in time. The suitability of the plot, for instance, comes before choosing the unit: if the plot allows nothing to enter the ground, half the solution types drop out from the start. Do I have to gather every figure in advance? No. To get your bearings, the name of the municipality, how the property is used and the size of the household are enough. Long absences and restarting What to do on the last day of use and on the first day back — and what already needs a specialist. Three different situations

reszek.cim: „A longer absence” is not one single state
reszek.szoveg: „A longer absence” is not one single state A two-week summer break, a three-month winter shutdown, and a property occupied one weekend a month all year round each have different consequences. The aim is that before buying you know what the chosen system asks of you — it should not emerge later from the operating manual. The last day of use

reszek.cim: What is worth doing before you leave
reszek.szoveg: What is worth doing before you leave What follows are general principles. The specific steps are always laid down by the unit's own current operating manual — and they differ from model to model. 01 The system does not have to be drained. The water left in the tank protects the structure and preserves the biological community. 02 With an active system, switching the aeration off entirely should be avoided. For a planned absence the controller offers a holiday mode — the operating manual describes how to set it. 03 Do not put anything into the system out of the ordinary in the final days — disinfectant, paint, large quantities of fat. 04 Check the cover and the ventilationbefore leaving it alone for a longer period. The first day back

reszek.cim: What is worth checking on arrival
reszek.szoveg: What is worth checking on arrival 01 Power and compressor. With an active system, the first check: is there power, and is the compressor running quietly and evenly. 02 Give the system time. Full treatment efficiency does not return on the first day; during that time the quality of the outlet water is temporarily poorer. 03 Avoid a sudden peak load in the first days — do not schedule a large gathering for the opening of the season. 04 With a septic tank system the manufacturer may recommend a refreshing bacterial additive after a longer break; follow the instructions for the particular product. 05 If there is odour, foaming or cloudiness do not wait: these are signals, not settling-in symptoms. Who does what

reszek.cim: The owner's task and the specialist's
reszek.szoveg: The owner's task and the specialist's What you can do yourself setting holiday mode as described in the operating manual; a visual check: cover, ventilation, the sound of the compressor; dosing the additive where the manufacturer prescribes it; keeping the usage log — particularly useful during an absence. What needs a specialist a persistent odour or a deviation in water quality after the restart; a fault indication on the controller; restarting after a complete shutdown of the system; suspected frost damage at a winterised property. reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.szoveg: Mains sewer or a standalone system? This question has to be settled BEFORE the technology is chosen. It is not a matter of opinion, and the pipe in the street does not decide it — official information does. In the reverse order, you find out mid-project that it cannot be built.

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: This page touches on a legal question
reszek.szoveg: This page touches on a legal question The information below is general, and the regulations may change. For the answer that applies to your own property from the regional water utility and the competent local authority is what you have to obtain — no website substitutes for that, ours included. Legal content last reviewed by a specialist: 9 August 2026 The review was based on the text available in the National Legislation Register, Government Decree 147/2010 (IV. 29.) as currently in force. The legal framework

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.szoveg: Two conditions the decree names Under Government Decree 147/2010 (IV. 29.), what carries particular weight is whether, on the public land bordering the property, the sewerage works are whether it is technically available, and whether there is adequate treatment plant capacity. If both conditions are met Under the decree no new wastewater treatment unit may be installed. This is not a matter of preference and price does not decide it: connection is the route. We will say so even when it means you will not be buying from us. If either is not met The next question opens up: which on-site solution suits the property? That does not yet mean a biological system, a septic tank or any particular unit will be right — the conditions of the plot and the use have to be examined next. Environmental conditions affect the installation requirements too: the regulations treat highly sensitive with regard to subsurface waters, and in high groundwater areas separately. In certain cases a municipal wastewater programme, a water base protection condition or further investigation may come into play — so for a specific property, information from the local authority, a designer or the authority may also be needed. The real question

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: It is not whether there is a pipe in the street
reszek.szoveg: It is not whether there is a pipe in the street In everyday speech, „there is a sewer” means a manhole is visible nearby. The regulations, however, work with a different concept: the technical availability of the sewerage works and adequate treatment plant capacity count together. The distinction has a practical consequence: if both hold, installing a new standalone treatment unit is not a viable route — it is not a matter of preference. If they do not, the standalone route is open. Hence the right order: first establish the mains sewer position, then choose the technology. The other way round, you find out mid-project that it cannot be built. What you see first, and what actually has to be established What you see first What is actually worth establishing Is there a pipe in the street? Is it technically available for the property? Is the neighbour connected? What conditions apply to your property? Does the neighbour have their own system? When was it built, and on what conditions? Does the sewer seem far away? What is the official technical connection position? The example of a neighbouring property, a utility map, or where the pipe visibly runs therefore gives no reliable answer on its own for your project. What to check

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: Four questions, and who to ask
reszek.szoveg: Four questions, and who to ask You need official answers to these. The neighbour's experience and the wording of a listing are not enough. 01 Are the sewerage works technically available on the public land bordering the property? Ask: the regional water utility. 02 Is there adequate treatment plant capacity? This can be a constraint even when the pipe is physically there. Ask: the utility. 03 Is the network planned, and when? Ask for a binding schedule, not verbal information. Ask: the local authority. 04 Does a water base protection or other restriction apply to the area? This can override every other consideration. Ask: the competent authority or the local council. Results

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: Four outcomes — every one of them valid
reszek.szoveg: Four outcomes — every one of them valid 01 The mains sewer is not available. The standalone route is open; the next task is to gather the plot and load data. 02 The mains sewer is available. Connection is then the route. We will say so even when it means you will not be buying from us. 03 Construction is scheduled and the date is known. It is worth comparing the connection and service charges with the full life-cycle cost of a standalone system. Waiting is a legitimate decision. 04 There is no clear answer. This is the most common outcome. The next task is then to obtain official information — and that we can help with. Cost

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: What is worth comparing — without a specific price
reszek.szoveg: What is worth comparing — without a specific price 01 On the mains sewer side: the connection fee, building the pipe run within the plot, and the ongoing service charge. 02 On the standalone system side: the investment, earthworks, energy, sludge handling and maintenance. 03 The time horizon decides it. The service charge runs for decades; with a standalone system it is avoided, but an operating duty remains in its place. The two sides can only be compared over the same period. The order

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.szoveg: Two gates, not one Settling the mains sewer position is only the first gate. If the standalone route is open, it does not yet follow which system you need. 01 Can standalone treatment be considered at all? Official information from the water utility and the local authority answers this — on the basis of technical availability and treatment plant capacity. 02 Which standalone solution suits the project? Here what decides is permanent or intermittent use, the expected occupancy and load, the free area of the plot, the soil, the groundwater and the disposal of the treated water. The decree itself names the characteristics of the soil, the depth of the subsurface water and the quantity of wastewater in connection with sizing and construction. While that data is still missing, choosing a specific unit would be premature. Cost

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: The two routes build their costs differently
reszek.szoveg: The two routes build their costs differently „Which is cheaper?” cannot be answered reliably in general without knowing the property's data. What makes the comparison meaningful is working through the same items on both routes. What belongs to one route and what to the other Mains sewer route Standalone system route Connection Unit or system Construction work required Earthworks and installation Arrangement within the plot Building the disposal arrangement for the treated water Long-term service charges Energy, emptying or sludge handling, maintenance, servicing In both cases the actual costs are affected considerably by the particular property and the technical arrangement it requires. So it is worth asserting neither in general that „the mains sewer is cheaper” nor that „you are better off with your own system”. Frequently asked questions

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: What is not worth deciding on assumption
reszek.szoveg: What is not worth deciding on assumption If there is a sewer in the street, is connection compulsory? Without knowing the property's current technical and legal position, a general yes or no is not worth giving. What has to be checked is the actual availability of the mains sewer and the conditions attached — with the utility and the local authority. Can I have my own treatment unit if there is a sewer in the street? That there is a pipe in the street does not give the whole answer on its own. For the regulations, the technical availability and the adequate treatment plant capacity matter too: if both hold, installing a new unit is not a viable route. What if the sewer is built later? It is worth checking how firm and how documented the development is, and how it fits the timing of your build or your use of the property. A general development plan or a verbal promise does not carry the same certainty as a documented, scheduled project. What if the sewer is too far away? „Too far” is everyday language, not a technical decision criterion. The actual possibility of connection is worth judging from official or utility information, not from how far you can see. Next step

reszek.lap: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.cim: If the standalone route is open
reszek.szoveg: If the standalone route is open The next task is to gather the data on your own situation. You do not have to know everything — the page shows where each figure can be obtained, which may be estimated, and where „I do not know” is an acceptable answer. Or let us talk it through Which data has to be gathered?

No mains sewer available For a proportion of occupied properties in Hungary there is no mains sewer, and there will not be one within any foreseeable time. The wastewater then has to be dealt with within the plot — but how matters. This page works through which solutions are in play, when each drops out, and what has to be established for them. Options

What options are there? There are four directions. What decides the choice first is not the price but where the treated water can go and what the local regulations allow. 01 Biological wastewater treatment unit. It treats the wastewater within the plot, and the treated water can be soaked away or — where the conditions are met — put to use. For permanent occupation this is the most common solution. It needs electricity, and regular but light operating attention. 02 Septic tank system with a soakaway. A simpler solution with no power requirement. It only works where the permeability of the soil is adequate and the groundwater sits deep enough — and the soakaway field takes up a considerable area. 03 Sealed holding tank. It does not treat, only collects: the wastewater has to be taken away regularly. Its place is where local conditions allow nothing at all to enter the ground. We do not manufacture this solution, but we will say so when that is the situation. 04 Waiting for the mains sewer. If the local authority has a firm, scheduled development plan and a connection is available within a foreseeable time, waiting with an interim solution may be worthwhile. A promise and a schedule, however, are not the same thing. Weighing it up

reszek.cim: Mains sewer or a standalone system?
reszek.szoveg: Mains sewer or a standalone system? It tips towards a standalone system if… there is no firm development schedule — the local authority cannot name a binding date; the connection point is far away, and the cost of the pipe run within the plot is significant on its own; the plot is suitable for disposing of the treated water, so the system can be closed off within the plot; you are planning for the long term: over the life of the system the service charge is avoided as well. It tips towards the mains sewer if… the network is being built and the connection date is known — a parallel investment is hard to justify in that case; the plot allows nothing to enter the ground, and there is no other way of disposing of the treated water; the main runs immediately next to the plot boundary, so the connection is technically straightforward; you intend to sell the property in the short term — there, the utility connection is itself an asset. Preparation

reszek.cim: Which data should be gathered first?
reszek.szoveg: Which data should be gathered first? With these answers we can already say which solutions are in play and which drop out — all before anyone visits the site. 01 The exact location of the property and the local regulations. The name of the municipality and the land registry number are enough to establish whether a water base protection or other restriction applies to the area. 02 How it is used, and by how many. Permanent occupation or intermittent use, how many people, and whether the load has a predictable peak (weekend guests, for instance). 03 The characteristics of the plot. Area, slope, the position of the built-up part, and where there is a free surface reachable by vehicle for the unit. 04 Soil and groundwater. An earlier geotechnical report or a drilled well data sheet helps a great deal. Failing that, the experience of neighbouring properties is a guide too. 05 What is intended to happen to the treated water. Whether there is a surface receiving water nearby (a ditch, a stream), whether you plan to reuse it for irrigation, and where the surrounding dug or drilled wells are. Missing data

reszek.cim: It is no problem if you do not yet have every figure
reszek.szoveg: It is no problem if you do not yet have every figure Most enquirers do not arrive already knowing the soil type, the groundwater situation, the depth of the pipe exit and the possible means of disposal. Nor do they need to. „I do not know” is not a wrong answer — it marks a piece of information still to be obtained. If you do not know this yet, here is where it can be found If you do not know this yet Where can it be found? What should the next step be? What is the soil like? From an existing document or an on-site investigation Pinning the figure down Where is the groundwater? From available data or from measurement Obtaining reliable information Is the mains sewer actually available? From the utility or from local information Clarifying the situation Where can the treated water go? From examining the plot conditions and the technical requirements Narrowing the options Good preparation does not mean you have to design the system. It is enough to know which questions remain to be settled. Check

reszek.cim: Settle these six things before you choose a system
reszek.szoveg: Settle these six things before you choose a system The first decision check needs no lengthy technical documentation. Start with these six questions. Is it settled that for the property no suitable mains sewer is available? Permanently or only intermittently is the property used? How many people normally use it, and what is the maximum load likely to be? How much usable area is available on the plot? What do you currently know about the soil and the groundwater? Is there any idea how to solve the onward disposal of the treated water? If several of these questions are still unanswered, that is no obstacle. They are precisely what shows which information is worth obtaining next. If, on the other hand, most of them are settled, comparing the solutions can become considerably more concrete. Cost

reszek.cim: The real cost does not end with the price of the unit
reszek.szoveg: The real cost does not end with the price of the unit „What does it cost?” is a fair question. But the prices of two different systems can only be compared meaningfully if we look beyond the moment of purchase. 01 The unit or system capital cost. 02 Installation and the earthworks required. 03 Any energy consumption — this depends on the technology. 04 Emptying or sludge handling according to how the system operates. 05 Routine maintenance. 06 Servicing needed later on. Their weight differs from solution to solution and from project to project. A lower opening figure therefore does not necessarily mean the better choice over the longer term. Specific prices are only worth comparing once the actual project data is known — guessed or generic figures found online lead easily to the wrong conclusion. Pitfalls

Typical mistakes in this situation 01 Choosing the unit before examining the plot. The most common ordering mistake. Even a good unit is unworkable if there is nowhere for the treated water to go. 02 Waiting on a promise. „It will be built within a few years” — without a schedule and funding this is not a figure you can plan on. Meanwhile the cost of emptying runs on. 03 Ignoring the neighbouring wells. Protective distances apply not only to your own abstraction points but to those on neighbouring properties too. 04 Counting only the capital cost. The full picture only comes together with operation: electricity consumption, sludge removal, maintenance — without these the solutions cannot be compared. Next step

Start with the situation assessment Once you roughly have the figures above, the decision aid will show from a few questions which solution types are in play in your case and which drop out — together with an order-of-magnitude cost range. The result is indicative: we give the final solution and price after an on-site survey. Or look first at the comparison of solution types Fill in the decision aid Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is connection to the mains sewer compulsory once it is built? Whether connection is compulsory, and by when, is a matter of local regulation and differs by municipality. It is worth establishing with the competent local authority or the utility before the works begin, because it affects the payback calculation. How long does installing a standalone system take? The installation itself usually takes a few days, but the overall lead time is governed by permitting and earthworks. We can give a realistic schedule after the survey, because the depth of the connection and the ground conditions affect it considerably. What happens if the sewer is built later after all? The installed system does not become worthless: reusing the treated water and avoiding the service charge can remain an advantage. What happens about connection and about the existing system is a matter of local regulation, however, so it is worth establishing in advance. Does a treatment unit smell? On odour it is not worth making a promise that holds in all circumstances. Several factors together govern how a properly chosen, installed and operated system behaves. If a persistent, abnormal smell appears, its cause has to be investigated — it is not inherent to the technology but a signal. Does it need emptying? That depends on the solution chosen and on how it works. With a sealed holding tank, removal is a fundamental part of operation; with other systems, sludge handling and emptying work differently. A precise frequency is only worth giving on the basis of verified system data and actual conditions of use. Does it need electricity? Not every wastewater solution works on the same principle.

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often (part 2)
reszek.szoveg: With active systems the energy demand is an important consideration; with other arrangements it may be different. What happens during a power cut? The answer depends on the system, so it has to be settled when the specific unit is chosen. Applying one general rule to every technology is not worth doing. Terms

reszek.cim: A few terms worth keeping apart
reszek.szoveg: A few terms worth keeping apart The technical terms matter, but on their own they do not help you decide. What counts is what they mean for your own property. Sealed holding tank It collects the wastewater produced; the accumulated volume has to be taken away. It does not treat, only collect. Septic tank system The septic tank together with the further treatment or disposal arrangement belonging to it together is how it should be understood. It is not simply a sealed tank under another name. Active biological treatment unit A system for treating wastewater on site, whose selection has to take account of both the load and the operating conditions. Drainage field The area belonging to a septic tank system that plays a part in how the whole system works — not an accessory but part of the technology. Standalone wastewater treatment An umbrella term for on-site solutions outside the public sewer network. The specific technical and legal categories always have to be settled for the project at hand. Where to go next

reszek.cim: From here, three separate questions are worth pursuing
reszek.szoveg: From here, three separate questions are worth pursuing You do not have to follow all three at once. It is worth going on where the uncertainty is greatest at the moment. You still want to understand the solution types The next step is a more detailed comparison of the sealed holding tank, the septic tank system and active biological treatment — against the same criteria. What options are there?→ A standalone system may not be an option The position on the mains sewer and the local conditions is worth establishing first. That is a legal question too, not only a technical one. Mains sewer or a standalone system?→ You are ready to prepare your own project It is worth gathering the key data on the property, the use and the plot — that already makes for a concrete conversation.
