On-site survey The survey is not a sales ritual but a technical service: it closes specific uncertainties. If the plot data is known you can go on without one — and we will say so. When it is worth having

Not every project needs one An on-site survey is not a compulsory step and not a sales ritual. It is worth having when it closes a specific uncertainty — one that paperwork cannot answer. If the plot data is known and shows no risk, the project can be prepared with photographs and documents. If the critical figures are missing or contradictory, however, a survey is the quickest route. Decision table

What is enough, and when 01 Documents and photographs are enough where the groundwater is known, the water disposal is settled, the depth of the pipe exit is given, and there is enough free area. 02 A survey is warranted where the groundwater or the water disposal is unknown, the slope is problematic, the wastewater pipe is deep, the free area is small, or the position of the system is uncertain. 03 It is effectively indispensable where a choice has to be made between several technical arrangements, or where the data contradicts itself. 04 A different expert is needed where the question is hydrogeological or geotechnical — a survey does not substitute for that. On site

reszek.cim: What we examine — and what we do not
reszek.szoveg: What we examine — and what we do not What we look at the position and depth of the wastewater pipe; the ground slope and the levels; the surface character of the soil and the visible water conditions; the free area and where the system could sit; the direction in which the treated water would be disposed of; access for installation and for later servicing; whether an additional technical element is needed — a pumping station, for instance. What it does NOT establish the design groundwater level — that needs an expert report; the numerical permeability of the soil; whether it can be permitted — that is a matter for the authority; the final price — that follows from the settled data. The result

What you receive Not a „personalised quote” but a structured plot brief — usable even if you end up buying elsewhere. 01 The proposed position of the system on the plot. 02 Connection levels — a gravity or a pumped solution. 03 The proposed direction for disposing of the treated water. 04 The critical risks named. 05 The additional technical elements required. 06 What is still missing — and which expert can supply it. With the architect and the mechanical engineer

reszek.cim: The brief can serve as a design input too
reszek.szoveg: The brief can serve as a design input too The connection levels and the position of the system are figures the architect and the mechanical designer need. Available early in the design, they save a later riser, a retrofitted pumping station or some other makeshift. Survey

Request an on-site survey Write and tell us where the property is and what you know about it — we will come back on whether a survey is warranted or whether the data lets you go on without one. If you would rather gather the data yourself, the checklist will walk you through it. Or start with the plot data checklist Request a survey
Plants and special loads The wastewater of office staff and wastewater from a production process are not the same task — even when the headcount is the same.

„Plant” is not a sizing category Treating the domestic wastewater of office staff and treating wastewater from a production process are entirely different projects — even when the headcount is the same. The regulations too treat used water arising from production and service activities as a wastewater category in its own right, and may set discharge limits specific to the industry and the pollutant. So the composition of the wastewater cannot be derived from headcount or from the daily volume of water. The first step

Separate the two water streams This is the single most important decision on this page — and in many cases the cheapest solution too. 01 Sanitary, domestic stream. The staff washroom, changing room and kitchen. Domestic in composition, it can be treated in the usual way. 02 Process stream. Water from production, washing and rinsing. Its composition is set by the technology, and it typically requires pre-treatment. 03 Why separation is worth it. The domestic stream is straightforward to treat; the process stream receives its own pre-treatment, sized accordingly. Treated together, the whole volume has to be designed to the stricter requirement. What you need to provide

The process data sheet 01 The activity carried out on the site. What is made, and by what processes. 02 Raw and ancillary materials. What may enter the water. 03 Number of shifts and operating days per year. 04 Seasonality. A winery produces something entirely different at harvest than in winter — seasonality is what sets the peak load. 05 Daily and maximum volume of water. Average and peak m³/day, and the hourly or per-shift peak. 06 Process wash and rinse waters. When, how much, of what composition. 07 Chemicals in use. Cleaning agents, disinfectants and process chemicals. 08 Wastewater temperature. Where relevant — it affects the biological process. 09 Laboratory results. BOD5, COD, suspended solids; depending on the industry, fats and oils, nitrogen, phosphorus, pH and other components. The exact list is set by the technology. 10 Existing pre-treatment. Screen, grease trap, settling tank, balancing tank. What you will not get from this page

And why not There is no capacity table here and no model recommendation. Where there is no representative laboratory data, the website does not attempt an automatic system recommendation — the natural next step is sampling and an expert feasibility study. Our earlier material mentioned the biological treatment of abattoir, dairy and winery wastewater as achievable. That professional capability may well exist, but no automatic sizing can be built on it on a website: the inlet water quality and the pre-treatment required differ from project to project. Until there is a project we can show with its inlet wastewater characteristics, pre-treatment, technology, discharge requirements, laboratory results and operating history, the correct wording is this: special loads can be handled on the basis of individual engineering analysis and design. This is not timidity. A badly sized industrial system does not waste the investor's money first — it makes meeting the discharge requirements impossible, and that is considerably harder to correct after the fact. Next step

reszek.cim: Let us start with the technology
reszek.szoveg: Let us start with the technology Write and tell us what the activity is, over how many shifts, in what annual rhythm, and whether there are already laboratory results. From that we can say whether the existing data is sufficient or whether sampling has to come first. Special or industrial wastewater Technical project brief Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often We have no laboratory results. Can we still request a quote? Not a quote, responsibly, but a feasibility discussion yes. From the technology, the working pattern and the flow we can say what analysis is needed and what order of magnitude is involved. For sizing, laboratory data is unavoidable. Which laboratory parameters are needed? The minimum is typically BOD5, COD and suspended solids; beyond that, depending on the industry, fats and oils, nitrogen, phosphorus, pH and temperature. The exact list is set by the technology — which is why we ask about the production process first. Is there anything you will not take on? Yes, and we say so in advance. There are process wastewaters that cannot be treated biologically, or only with substantial pre-treatment. Where that is the case we say so during the feasibility study — not after the quote. Can the staff wastewater be treated separately? In many plants yes, and it is often the cheapest solution. It is worth examining at the design stage, because separating the network afterwards is substantial work.

Plot data checklist This is not a form: it asks for no contact details and assumes nothing about wanting a quote. You can go through it on your own, and at the end you will see what you have and what is missing — „I do not know” is a valid answer. How you use it

It asks nothing of you This list not a form: it asks for no contact details and assumes nothing about wanting a quote. You can go through it on your own, and at the end you will see what you have and what is missing. Four answers are possible for each item: known · estimated · not known · must be measured. An estimated figure, one taken from a document and one actually measured are not equally reliable — and so they suffice for different things. If you later request a quote, that difference matters. „I do not know” is not a failure. Beside every item stands where it can be obtained. Basics

Basic data Data How necessary Where it can be obtained Municipality, address, land registry number required title deed, listing Mains sewer situation required water utility, local authority Size of the plot required title deed, map extract Layout

reszek.cim: What follows from what is missing
reszek.szoveg: What follows from what is missing 01 Every required figure is in place. The project can go on: the discussion with the designer or the preparation of a quote can follow. 02 The groundwater or the soil is missing. This is the most common case. The next step is obtaining an expert report — or, if one is being prepared for the build anyway, extending it to this question. 03 The depth of the pipe exit not known. On a new build it can be asked of the mechanical designer; at an existing house it can be established by excavating. 04 Water disposal is uncertain. This is the point where an on-site survey is the quickest route — paperwork cannot settle it. Saving
Fillable version The fillable, saveable version is still being built. Until then the tables above can be printed or saved from the browser, and used that way in a discussion. Next step

reszek.cim: If any question is still open
reszek.szoveg: If any question is still open An on-site survey is worth having when it closes a specific uncertainty — it is not a sales ritual. The next page shows when it is warranted, and when documents and photographs are enough. On-site survey
Plot suitability The pipe level, the groundwater and the water disposal are interrelated conditions. And plot suitability is not product suitability — the two are not the same. The real question

reszek.cim: It is not whether it fits
reszek.szoveg: It is not whether it fits Plot suitability is not geometry. The wastewater pipe coming from the house, its level, the ground slope, the soil, the groundwater, the space available and the disposal of the treated water interrelated technical conditions — none of them can be settled without the others. And one important distinction: the plot suitability is not product suitability. That the plot is suitable in principle does not mean any particular unit can be installed on it unaltered. What most often changes the design

reszek.cim: Four conditions that change the configuration
reszek.szoveg: Four conditions that change the configuration These typically do not rule anything out — but they call for a different arrangement, which moves the cost too. 01 The depth of the inlet pipe. If the wastewater pipe arrives deeper than the unit's inlet level allows, a riser or a pumping station may be needed. This is worth settling at the design stage of the house. 02 High or fluctuating groundwater. Not a yes or no question: it can change how the tank is installed, and has to be examined separately whether the treated water can be disposed of — the two are not the same. 03 Vehicle loading. If a car stands or drives over the cover, that affects the arrangement. 04 Access for installation and servicing. What is tight at installation stays tight for later maintenance. Four outcomes

The pre-screening issues no „suitable” stamp 01 Standard. The data is known and shows no risk. 02 Conditional. Feasible, but with a different arrangement. 03 Further data is needed. Typically the groundwater or the pipe level is missing. This is the most common outcome, and it is not bad news. 04 On-site survey is what is needed. The data contradicts itself, or the plot is not technically standard. If you do not know

reszek.cim: On unknown groundwater we issue no verdict of „suitable”
reszek.szoveg: On unknown groundwater we issue no verdict of „suitable” If the groundwater or the disposal of the treated water is unknown, no suitability verdict follows from it — neither yes nor no. The right answer then is what has to be obtained, and from where. At the same time, not every non-standard plot is ruled out: a deep pipe exit, high groundwater and some slopes can be handled with a different installation arrangement. Next step

reszek.cim: What size of system is needed?
reszek.szoveg: What size of system is needed? Capacity does not follow straight from the number of occupants — water consumption, the peaks and the expected change count too. Or the cost of the whole project Capacity and occupancy

Project starter / situation assessment The practical end point of the hub. It makes no final technical decision and gives no price — it shows what you have, what is missing, and what the next sensible step is. It is a valid result too if you are not yet ready to request a quote. What it gives you and what it does not

reszek.cim: It gives an assessment of the situation, not a quotation
reszek.szoveg: It gives an assessment of the situation, not a quotation The situation assessment translates the general knowledge to your own property. It does not make a final technical decision, and gives no price. What it does give: which figures you have, which are missing, what the main risks are, and what the next sensible step is. The result is useful even when it turns out you are not yet ready to request a quote — especially then. How it asks

reszek.cim: It adapts to what you already know
reszek.szoveg: It adapts to what you already know The owner of a holiday home is asked different questions than someone buying a plot. Anyone who has not yet bought the plot is not asked something they cannot answer. 01 Where you are in the project. Getting your bearings, looking at plots, designing, or already requesting a quote. 02 What the property is and how it is used. Type, permanent or intermittent use, occupancy, peak load. 03 What the present situation is. Whether there is already a system on the plot, and what you know about the mains sewer. 04 What you know about the plot. Area, soil, groundwater, disposal of the treated water, the depth of the pipe — as much as you know. 05 What it does not tud. „I do not know” is an answer of its own, not a field left blank: it is what the list of missing data is built from. The result

reszek.cim: Five outcomes, every one of them a sensible continuation
reszek.szoveg: Five outcomes, every one of them a sensible continuation 01 Gather this data — a specific list of what is missing and where it can be obtained. 02 Check the plot's suitability — what can be built is decided by the plot's characteristics. 03 Request an on-site survey — where the open questions can only be answered on site. 04 Consult an expert — in a complex or non-domestic situation. 05 You are ready to request a quote — this appears only when everything needed is genuinely in place. Missing data

reszek.cim: „I do not know” is not a wrong answer — it marks a task
reszek.szoveg: „I do not know” is not a wrong answer — it marks a task A pre-qualification helps when it does not force you to guess. Missing information is useful data in itself: it shows what still has to be settled, and with whom. If this is not known, this may be the next task If this is not known The next task might be Mains sewer position Obtaining official information from the water utility and the local authority Depth of the wastewater pipe Checking the drawings or the contractor's records, measuring if needed Groundwater Checking an existing document, further investigation if needed Exact plot data A drawing, a measurement or an on-site survey The exact route always depends on which information is missing and which decision would need it. The point is that a technical conclusion which looks certain should not be born of an uncertain estimate. The line

reszek.cim: Where the automation stops and a specialist takes over
reszek.szoveg: Where the automation stops and a specialist takes over A situation assessment is reliable when it knows exactly how far its remit runs. The disqualifying circumstances, the capacity limits and the situations that call for a survey have to be from approved rules judged — not left to automation running free. What the automation helps with putting a free-text description of the situation in order; summarising the missing data in plain language; making sure only the relevant questions appear. reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.szoveg: I want to replace an existing cesspit Replacement is the right decision when the survey supports it. Sometimes the old system can run for years yet; sometimes replacement is an unavoidable step that has been put off for years. This page works through how to decide — beyond the emptying invoice. Decision

reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.szoveg: When is replacement warranted? Replacement is indicated if… the emptying frequency is rising, or its cost is already comparable to the repayments on an investment; the system smells, backs up or leaks — these are not operating trifles but signs of a structural or capacity problem; the cesspit is of a leaching design, so untreated wastewater is entering the ground — in most places today this is not a tenable state of affairs; an extension or a refurbishment is planned, and the load is going to increase; the concrete structure has aged: cracking, settlement, a collapsed cover. Replacement is not urgent if… the system is sealed and sound, and the emptying frequency has been steady for years; construction of the mains sewer is scheduled, and the connection will happen within a foreseeable time; the property is rarely used, and the load is a fraction of that of permanent occupation; the problem can be narrowed to a single element — to the cover or the connecting pipe, for instance — because a repair may then be enough. Terms

reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.cim: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system?
reszek.szoveg: Cesspit, septic tank or biological system? The three are not three variants of the same thing. They work differently, their outputs differ, and they are tied to different conditions. 01 Cesspit (sealed holding tank). It does not treat, only collects. The whole volume of wastewater has to be taken away, so the running cost rises in proportion to water consumption. Old cesspits of a leaching design also let untreated wastewater into the ground. 02 Septic tank with a soakaway. It carries out mechanical pre-treatment, after which the partly treated water passes to a soakaway field. It needs no electricity, but the permeability of the soil and the groundwater level constrain it, and the soakaway field takes a considerable area. 03 Biological wastewater treatment unit. It genuinely cleans the wastewater, so the treated water can be disposed of over a considerably smaller area and, in favourable cases, put to use. It needs electricity and calls for regular — but light — operating attention. Cost

reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.szoveg: Total cost and payback The two solutions can only be compared by looking at the total cost of each. For an existing cesspit that is chiefly the charge for regular emptying, which grows with the household's water consumption and rises with the service tariffs. With a biological system, alongside the capital cost come electricity consumption, periodic sludge removal and maintenance — together considerably lower than continuous emptying, but not nil. Payback can therefore be calculated not in general but from the particular household's consumption figures. On the capital side the price of the unit is often not the largest item: the earthworks, the depth of the connection, decommissioning the old cesspit and the method of disposing of the treated water together move the total considerably. That is why we give a range rather than a quote until there has been a survey. Survey

reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.szoveg: Assessing the existing system Before replacement the old system has to be examined too — not only to establish whether replacement is warranted, but because decommissioning it is part of the project. 01 The type and condition of the existing structure. Sealed or leaching in design, what material it is made of, whether the structure is sound, and how deep it is. 02 The actual load. The water consumption figures and the emptying frequency together show what capacity is actually needed. 03 The route and depth of the connecting pipe. This decides whether the new unit can go where the old one was, or whether a pumping station is needed. 04 What becomes of the old cesspit. The method of decommissioning — emptying, possibly backfilling or demolition — is a permitting question too, and a cost item. 05 Disposal of the treated water. The new system's output has to have somewhere to go; this is the most important point of the survey, because without it the replacement cannot be planned. Next step

reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.cim: Cost and project brief for the replacement
reszek.szoveg: Cost and project brief for the replacement From a few questions, the decision aid shows whether replacement is warranted in your case, which solution types are in play, and what order of cost to reckon with. The module gives no quotation: the result is indicative and the data from an on-site survey can override it. reszek.lap: I want to replace an existing cesspit
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Can the new unit go where the old cesspit was? Sometimes yes, but that is not the default. The size, depth and condition of the old structure and the route of the connecting pipe decide it. We look at this specifically at the survey, because the answer affects the cost of the earthworks considerably. What happens to the old cesspit? It has to be emptied, and what becomes of it — backfilling or demolition — is decided by the local requirements and the circumstances of the installation. This is part of the project and a cost item, so it appears separately in the quote. How long does the replacement take, and can the property be lived in meanwhile? The installation itself usually takes a few days. Use of the property is restricted briefly, chiefly while the connection is being run through. We give the exact schedule after the survey, because the volume of earthworks determines it.

Restaurants and commercial kitchens The number of covers is not enough here. Kitchen water differs in composition from domestic effluent — and that is precisely what determines what goes ahead of the biological stage. The first thing to say

reszek.cim: The number of covers is not enough here
reszek.szoveg: The number of covers is not enough here In sizing a restaurant or commercial kitchen, the number of covers is not enough on its own, because the used water arising from the kitchen composition may differ from purely domestic wastewater. The regulations also treat wastewater from production and service activities separately: the pollutants characteristic of the discharge, the technological limits and the pre-treatment required all have to be examined on their own. So here the project becomes an engineering question early — and that is not complication but the condition of a working system. Two separate wastewater streams

What is worth keeping apart Sanitary — guests and staff Washroom, WC, handbasin Domestic in composition Proportional to the number of covers Conventional biological treatment handles it Typically requires no pre-treatment Kitchen — the water from cooking and washing up Washing up, preparation, cleaning A higher organic, fat and oil load Proportional to the number of meals and the kitchen's operating hours With short, intense peaks May require pre-treatment — typically grease separation What you need to provide

The kitchen load data sheet 01 The type of facility. Restaurant, inn, buffet, event venue, hotel or institutional kitchen. 02 Average and maximum number of covers per day. Or, in an institutional kitchen, the number of portions per day. 03 Opening hours and the kitchen's operating hours. The kitchen peak is typically shorter and more intense than the flow of guests. 04 Event or seasonal peak. Mekkora, which gyakori, how long tart. 05 The type of cooking. Fatty and fried dishes, large-scale preparation — these mean a different load. 06 The dishwashing technology. By hand, by machine, conveyor dishwasher — different volumes of water and use of chemicals. 07 Existing grease separator. If there is one: type, size, frequency of maintenance. 08 Actual water use. In an operating business this is the most reliable figure. On grease separation

reszek.cim: What we do not assert in general
reszek.szoveg: What we do not assert in general A heavy kitchen grease load is indeed a typical reason for pre-treatment, and for the wastewater of certain activities the regulations prescribe it. What we cannot do, however, not assert that the same grease trap requirement applies to every restaurant. Whether one is needed, in what size and in what arrangement, has to be derived from how that particular kitchen operates and — where available — from measurements. Grease, incidentally, is not a theoretical problem: it forms a film on the surface and impairs the oxygen transfer, so it reduces the efficiency of the biological stage directly. It is therefore not worth putting off on a „we shall see” basis. Next step

reszek.cim: Let us start with the kitchen figures
reszek.szoveg: Let us start with the kitchen figures Sizing the kitchen load is worth involving an expert in early. The project brief gathers what is needed for it. Pre-treatment and accessories Technical project brief Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is a grease trap compulsory? We do not assert it in general. The regulations prescribe pre-treatment for the wastewater of certain activities, and a kitchen grease load is a typical reason — but whether one is needed in your business, and in what size, has to be derived from how the kitchen operates. We examine this on the specific project. Can the kitchen and guest wastewater be separated? In many businesses yes, and it is often the cheapest solution: the sanitary stream can be treated in the usual way while the kitchen stream receives separate pre-treatment. It is worth examining at the design stage — retrofitting is considerably harder. Is a laboratory analysis needed? With a larger kitchen load, typically yes. Without it the sizing would rest on assumption, and precisely on the riskiest item. The cost of the analysis is a fraction of what putting right an under-sized system costs. We have accommodation alongside the restaurant. Then two load profiles come together: the accommodation one and the kitchen one. They have to be stated separately and handled separately in the sizing — the two do not simply add up.
Schools and institutions The 300 people do not use the facility all at once, all day, or all year. So the nominal headcount misleads on its own. A different rhythm

reszek.cim: An institution's load is not that of a dwelling
reszek.szoveg: An institution's load is not that of a dwelling A school's or an institution's load varies differently from a family home's or an accommodation business's: a strong weekday daytime peak, a drop at weekends and longer holidays all occur. So the nominal number of pupils or staff misleads on its own. The 300 people do not use the facility all at once, all day, or all year. What you need to provide

The institutional operating profile 01 Type of institution. School, nursery, office, social care institution, community building, sports facility. 02 Nominal and actual headcount. How many are on the register, and how many are typically present. 03 Hours of use per day. How many hours they spend there. A nursery child present for four hours is not the same load as a resident. 04 Weekend use. Whether there is any, and to what extent. 05 Holidays and operating days per year. Summer and winter holidays — these are long periods of underload. 06 Catering. Whether there is a production kitchen, how many portions, over what hours. If there is, that is a separate stream. 07 Sport, events, residential use. A gym with showers, evening events, a boarding house — each a separate window of load. 08 Actual water use. For an existing institution this is available, and it is considerably more accurate than any estimate. On the commercial kitchen

reszek.cim: It cannot be folded into the headcount
reszek.szoveg: It cannot be folded into the headcount If the institution has a production kitchen, its wastewater has to be treated as a separate commercial kitchen load stream it has to be treated — not simply added to the headcount. Its composition differs, its distribution over time differs, and it may require pre-treatment. A school with a kitchen and one without, of the same size, are two different projects. Operation is an organisational question

reszek.cim: „Anyone can pick it up” is not enough
reszek.szoveg: „Anyone can pick it up” is not enough At institutional scale, operation is not a side activity. Even for standalone systems the regulations require regular checks, an operating log, maintenance and in certain cases sampling — and on a larger project an even clearer regime of operating responsibility is needed. So on an institutional project the following have to be settled in advance: ki the named person responsible, what training they receive, who covers for them during holidays and leave, who keeps the documentation, and what service arrangement goes with it. This is a decision for the operator of the institution, not a technical detail — and it is typically where an otherwise well-designed institutional system stalls. Next step

reszek.cim: Let us settle the operating model too
reszek.szoveg: Let us settle the operating model too With an institutional system, monitoring and operation are questions to settle before the quote. The page on this in the Solutions section works through it in detail. Technical project brief Monitoring and operation Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often The school has 300 pupils. What system is needed? That single figure cannot settle it. It also takes the actual daily attendance, the hours spent there, the operating days per year, the holidays, and whether there is a production kitchen. At an existing institution the water consumption approximates all of this well — that is where to start. What happens over the summer holidays? A long period of underload arises, and it has to be managed. This is a question of operating mode and of choice of technology, and it counts in the sizing too: the system has to withstand the holiday state as well, not only term time. Who will operate it? That is for the operator of the institution to decide, and it is worth doing at the design stage. A named person responsible is needed, with training, cover and a documentation regime. This is often an organisational question, not a technical one. We are in a public procurement process. Defining the technical content precisely is then particularly important, because the comparability of the bids turns on it. We are glad to help put the technical specification together — write and tell us where the process stands.

Seasonal case studies At a seasonal property the risk at purchase is years of operation. So documented cases with a similar pattern of use say the most — not photographs. Why this is not a photo gallery

reszek.cim: The rhythm of use is the evidence
reszek.szoveg: The rhythm of use is the evidence At a seasonal property the question is not whether the installation looks good but whether it has been running for years under the same pattern of useas the one you are planning. So each case carries the type of property, the annual pattern of use, the longest absence, the plot's characteristics, the system chosen, the reason for the choice and the year of installation — not just a picture and a quote. Cases

Seasonal case studies The case library is being put together. For a seasonal property we publish no case until the multi-year operating data — season- opening tasks, servicing needed, actual maintenance — is available for it. A photograph and a quote are not evidence in this area. Intermittently used properties make up a substantial share of the projects so far. If you would like to hear about a comparable case, write to us — we will tell you what we found. In the meantime
Build your own profile From a few questions, the usage profile shows which directions remain relevant to your pattern and what still has to be settled. Building a usage profile

Soil, groundwater and water disposal Most misunderstandings arise from treating whether the tank can be installed and whether the treated water can be disposed of as one question. They are two separate decisions — and the second is the harder one. The most common misunderstanding

Two separate decisions, not egy Whether the tank can be installed and whether the treated water can be disposed of two separate questions. That the tank can be anchored technically even in higher groundwater — with a concrete surround, for instance — does not followthat the water can be soaked away on site. That distinction is the most important thing to take from this page. Many projects stall because the two were treated as one question. Soil

reszek.cim: What counts is not the name of the soil but its permeability
reszek.szoveg: What counts is not the name of the soil but its permeability 01 Loose, sandy soil drains well: infiltration can work over a smaller area. 02 Cohesive, clayey soil drains poorly: infiltration either calls for a considerable area or is not a viable route. 03 The name of the soil type is not enough on its own. The same label can cover different permeabilities; sizing requires measurement. 04 Stratification matters too. Beneath the surface layer there may be an impermeable layer that prevents infiltration. Groundwater

reszek.cim: The seasonal maximum counts, not today's level
reszek.szoveg: The seasonal maximum counts, not today's level This is the most commonly misunderstood figure. A low level established by a summer measurement says nothing about the spring maximum. 01 The design level is what decides it. Both installing the tank and the possibility of infiltration are limited by the seasonal maximum. 02 Effect on the tank: in high groundwater, separate anti-flotation anchoring is needed. 03 Effect on infiltration: the treated water needs a sufficient layer of soil above the groundwater; this is independent of whether the tank can be installed. 04 Where it can be found: a geotechnical report, a drilled well data sheet, the neighbours' experience, and whether water stands on the plot in spring. Water disposal

reszek.cim: Where the treated water can go
reszek.szoveg: Where the treated water can go 01 Infiltration into the ground. The most common solution, but it depends on the permeability of the soil and the groundwater level. The soakaway field takes up a considerable area. 02 Surface receiving water. A ditch, a stream or a channel — if there is one nearby and its manager consents. 03 Reuse. For irrigation, for instance, where the conditions are met. 04 If none of these is possible, the sealed holding tank remains — we will say so even when our system does not follow from it. Obtaining the data

reszek.cim: What informal enquiry settles, and what needs measurement
reszek.szoveg: What informal enquiry settles, and what needs measurement Enough as orientation the neighbours' experience of the spring water level; observing the plot — does water stand anywhere, where is the low point; data sheets of nearby drilled wells, where available; the surface character of the soil at a spade's depth. Only measurement can establish the design groundwater level — that needs an expert report; permeability as a number; the stratification down to the depth of infiltration; the sizing of the soakaway field — this is calculated from the figures above. When an expert is needed

Some things cannot be estimated Bringing in a hydrogeologist or a geotechnical engineer is warranted where the groundwater is unknown or contradictory, where the plot lies in a water base protection or highly sensitive area, or where infiltration is a borderline case for the sizing. Next step

reszek.cim: More than a request for a quote
reszek.szoveg: More than a request for a quote An institution's or a business's wastewater load cannot be described with a few headcount and plot fields. So this page is not a general quotation request but a structured project data package. From it, it can be decided whether the project goes towards a standard configuration, detailed engineering sizing, an on-site survey, laboratory analysis or a separate feasibility study. The aim is that our specialist receives a structured decision situation rather than a raw enquiry of the „price for a 200-bed hotel please” kind — and that you are not told back that „this needs more data”. What the brief records

Six groups of data 01 Project identification. Type of facility, municipality, project stage, intended commissioning date, new or existing system. 02 Load. Nominal headcount or bed count, average daily occupancy, peak occupancy, average and maximum m³/day, operating days, seasonal curve, shifts. 03 The character of the wastewater. Purely domestic, commercial kitchen, process, or a mixture of several origins; existing laboratory results; existing pre-treatment. 04 Plot and receiving water. Available area, pipe levels, soil and groundwater, receiving water, mains sewer, existing network. 05 Technical readiness. Existing drawings, process water streams, headroom for expansion, monitoring requirements, redundancy requirements. 06 Operation. Responsible operator, maintenance model, service expectations, documentation, record-keeping, procurement process. The output

Documents With these we reach a technical direction considerably faster. We use your data solely to answer your enquiry. 01 Site plan 02 Mechanical drawings 03 A consumption series — water bills or meter readings 04 Laboratory results, where available 05 An earlier drawing or permit 06 An existing quote, if you would like a comparison For industrial wastewater

The result is then „expert examination required” — and that is not a refusal but the correct first step. reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Why do I not get a price straight away? Because on a business or institutional project a price quoted from capacity or bed count would mislead. The whole project and life-cycle cost is determined together by the system architecture, the pre-treatment, the installation, the monitoring and the operation. With a settled project scope, however, a price band can be given. How much data does an enquiry need? For a conversation, the type of facility and the scale are enough. To name a technical direction we need the load profile and the character of the wastewater. For a quote, the plot, the receiving water and the operating model on top of those. We are in a procurement process and need a technical specification. We are glad to help with that. Total cost and payback A claim of the „pays for itself in four years” kind always holds for one particular household and one particular year's charge. As a general promise it misleads — which is why we show a cost range and the uncertainties instead.

reszek.cim: Why we name no payback period
reszek.szoveg: Why we name no payback period A claim of the „pays for itself in four years” kind always holds for one particular household, one particular year's emptying charge and one particular installation. As a general promise it misleads: the emptying charge differs from one municipality to the next and changes yearly, while the installation cost is driven by the earthworks and the water disposal. So here we show a cost range and the uncertainties is what we show, not a payback period — and we name the figures without which no responsible economic conclusion can yet be drawn. The method

reszek.cim: Whole life cycle, not capital price
reszek.szoveg: Whole life cycle, not capital price The financial decision on replacement is not a comparison of the old system's annual emptying charge with the purchase price of the new unit. There are several items on each side — and the largest are not where you would look first. The right approach 5, 10 and 15-year scenarios, with a sensitivity check: what happens to the result if the emptying frequency, the energy price, the size of the household or the additional work required changes. The remaining period of use is an input too: someone planning five more years with the property gets a different result from someone planning twenty-five. The cost side

What documents may be needed? Not every document is needed for every project. The building control documentation, the technical drawings and any regulatory documentation serve different purposes — and different people ask for them. First, let us be clear

reszek.cim: Not every document is needed for every project
reszek.szoveg: Not every document is needed for every project Three different things are often confused: the building control documentation for the building, the drawings used for the technical preparation of the wastewater system, and any regulatory documentation for standalone wastewater treatment. These serve different purposes, and different people ask for them. So we give no universal list of documents. The breakdown below arranges by role what is worth obtaining from where. Roles

Who contributes what What the client gathers the address and land registry number of the plot title deed and map extract photographs of the plot and the access the intended number of occupants and, where known, the water consumption an earlier utility statement or permit, if any What is worth asking the designer for a site plan showing the layout of the building and the plot the intended exit point of the wastewater pipe and its depth ground levels and slope designation of the area intended for disposing of the treated water a geotechnical report, if one is being prepared for the build anyway What ÖkoTech uses the data above, for sizing and planning the installation the unit's technical data sheet a declaration of performance, where the procedure requires one What an authority or an expert may ask for depends on the location and size of the project, the method of water disposal and the sensitivity classification of the area and so there is no universal list of documents — the procedure has to be established for each project in turn Regulatory procedure

reszek.cim: Why we give no ready-made procedural template
reszek.szoveg: Why we give no ready-made procedural template The procedure required is determined together by the location and size of the project, the method of disposing of the treated water and the sensitivity classification of the area. The same unit can call for different procedures in two municipalities. Our earlier permit examples serve as illustrations, but not templates that apply automatically: each was issued at a particular time, in a particular municipality, for a particular type of project. When we release one, we release it with its date, municipality and project type precisely so that it cannot be used as a template. For a new dwelling, the requirements for building control documentation always have to be checked against the current building control rules; this area changes often. Next step

reszek.szoveg: „I do not know” is a valid answer too This list is not an exam. In the tables below, each figure carries why it matters, where it can be found, and that can be estimated-e or must be measured. If you do not know something, that is not a failure but information: it shows that the next step is obtaining a document, an on-site survey or bringing in an expert. An estimated figure, one taken from a document and one actually measured are not equally reliable — and so they suffice for different things. To get your bearings, the name of the municipality, how the property is used and the occupancy are enough. The rest becomes necessary at the sizing and quotation stage. Data quality

reszek.lap: Which data should be gathered first?
reszek.cim: Not every figure is equally certain — note where you know it from
reszek.szoveg: Not every figure is equally certain — note where you know it from The same number carries quite different weight depending on whether it was estimated from memory, appears on a drawing, or was actually measured. So it is worth noting the source beside every important figure — that is what shows what it suffices for. 01 Estimated. Enough for a first orientation on certain figures — the frequency of use or the approximate size of the free area already shows which questions have to be settled. Which estimates can be used for a later technical decision has to be decided separately. 02 Documented. Taken from a drawing, a utility statement or another document. Say what kind of document it is and how current — a statement issued ten years ago is not the same as last year's. 03 Measured. An actual measurement. For certain decisions — typically on groundwater and infiltration capacity — only this is acceptable; exactly where, is decided by the project and the technical question at hand. 04 Not known. Not an obstacle in itself. It helps us start from something other than an uncertain estimate and find the right next step instead. This answer moves things forward too. The distinction matters especially for groundwater, soil, pipe depth and the documents available. Where an uncertain estimate produces a technical conclusion that looks certain, the site will refute it later — typically at the most expensive moment. Data group

reszek.lap: Which data should be gathered first?
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often What if I do not know the groundwater? This is the most commonly missing figure, and it is no obstacle to getting your bearings. The design groundwater level can be established by measurement; if a geotechnical report is being prepared for the build anyway, it is worth asking for the wastewater aspects to be included — one investigation, answers to two questions. How much data is worth gathering before I contact you? You do not have to wait until you have everything. The name of the municipality, how the property is used and the occupancy are enough for us to say which directions are in play. The detailed figures are needed at the sizing stage. Is estimated data enough for a quote? For an order-of-magnitude indication yes, for a final quote no. The installation circumstances — earthworks, connection depth, water disposal — drive the total most, and these have to be measured, not estimated. I do not know how deep the wastewater pipe leaves the building. It is worth looking at the drawings or the construction documentation first. If the figure is not there either, measurement may be needed later. It is not for you to decide whether pumping is required, for instance — giving the underlying figure accurately is enough. I have no site plan. That does not in itself mean you cannot go on. For a first round a hand-drawn sketch helps, provided it shows the building, the plot boundary, the free area and the position of the well. An accurate drawing becomes necessary when the sizing and the siting become concrete. I do not know the water consumption. On a new build there is often no such figure — the occupancy and the pattern of use are then the starting point.

reszek.lap: Which data should be gathered first?
reszek.cim: What we are asked most often (part 2)
reszek.szoveg: If you do not know the consumption, write that it is unknown: a number given at random is worse than a missing one. When does a specialist have to be involved? Not every unknown calls immediately for a surveyor, a hydrogeologist or a designer. It is worth establishing first which information is missing and which decision it affects — after that it can be decided whether further measurement or an expert is needed. We have a separate page on this: when an expert is needed.

What does intermittent load mean? The same headcount can mean three different loads. The pattern of use describes it, not the number of people — and the longest gap is the strongest filter. The real question

reszek.cim: It is not how many people use it
reszek.szoveg: It is not how many people use it A four-person holiday home can mean three different things: a house used every weekend, a property occupied continuously from June to August, or a hunting lodge visited a few times a year. The same headcount, three different engineering tasks. So the load is described not by the number of people but by the pattern of use: when, how often and for how long wastewater is produced — and how long the longest complete break is. What has to be recorded

reszek.cim: Six figures that make a load profile
reszek.szoveg: Six figures that make a load profile Together these say more than the headcount on its own. 01 Which months the property is used. 02 How often you return — weekly, monthly, a few times a year. 03 The average length of a stay, and the longest continuous period of use. 04 The longest complete gap — this is the strongest filter on the choice of technology. 05 Typical and maximum occupancy, and how often the maximum occurs. 06 Whether there is power during the absence, and whether the building is winterised. Two different things

reszek.cim: Underload is not the same as zero load
reszek.szoveg: Underload is not the same as zero load Underload — little wastewater, but regular the biological community is fed, just sparingly; the system works and the efficiency is generally maintained; regular weekend use typically belongs here. Zero load — nothing for weeks the activity of the biological community falls off; the restart takes time; a long seasonal break belongs here — and this is what can override the choice of technology. An open question

Where exactly is the line? Precisely how long a gap counts as short and where a sustained break begins, we do not put in a specific duration until our own technical data supports it. A wrongly stated threshold would lead to the wrong choice of technology — and that is a decision for decades. At the survey, however, we can tell you for your own particular pattern of use. Next step

reszek.cim: The technology follows from the profile
reszek.szoveg: The technology follows from the profile Once the pattern of use is known, the conditions for the two directions can be compared — and it also becomes clear if the plot overrides the decision. Or build your usage profile Biological system or septic tank?

What options are there? With no mains sewer, the wastewater has to be dealt with on site — but that does not mean one single solution. There are four directions, and the choice is decided not by the unit but by the property, the plot and the local regulations together. The decision space

Four directions, not one product If the property cannot be connected to a mains sewer, the wastewater has to be dealt with on site — but that does not mean one single solution. There are four directions, and each has different conditions. The choice is decided not by the unit but by how the property is used, the expected load, the plot, the soil and groundwater conditions, the disposal of the treated water and the local regulations — together. Options

reszek.cim: What is in play, and on what condition
reszek.szoveg: What is in play, and on what condition The order is not a ranking. For each we set out what it does and what it takes for it to be in play at all. 01 Active biological treatment unit. With an energy input it genuinely cleans the wastewater. Its conditions are a continuous power supply, a regular load, and somewhere for the treated water to go. It calls for regular but light operating attention. 02 Septic tank system with a drainage field. The septic tank pre-treats; most of the treatment happens in the ground. It needs no electricity, but the drainage field takes a considerable area and the permeability of the soil is decisive. 03 Sealed holding tank. It does not treat, only collects: the whole volume has to be taken away. Its place is where local conditions allow nothing at all to enter the ground. We do not manufacture this, but we will say so when that is the situation. 04 Checking the mains sewer again, or waiting. If the network turns out to be technically available after all, or its construction is scheduled and the date known, a parallel investment is hard to justify. Use

reszek.cim: What tips it one way or the other
reszek.szoveg: What tips it one way or the other It tips towards active biological treatment if… the property is in permanent occupation, so the load is regular; the free area is limited — the drainage field would not fit here; there is a continuous power supply on the plot; you would put the treated water to use, for irrigation for instance. It tips towards the septic tank if… use is intermittent, with long stretches carrying no load; there is no power supply, or it is unreliable; the soil is well draining, and there is room for the drainage field; as little operating duty as possible is what you want, and you accept the larger area it takes. Method

reszek.cim: Work through the same criteria for all three
reszek.szoveg: Work through the same criteria for all three A comparison easily misleads if we look at price for one system, treatment technology for another and only footprint for the third. It is worth asking the same eight questions of each. How it works — what happens to the wastewater inside the system? Permanent or intermittent use are we looking for a solution? How much area does it need — not just the unit, the whole technical solution? What is its energy demand? What happens to the treated water inside the system and afterwards? What emptying or sludge handling duty remains? What maintenance does it require from the owner? What makes up the capital cost and the longer-term running cost? Seeing these side by side, you are no longer choosing between three products that are hard to compare but comparing three different modes of operation. We have also set the three systems against these same criteria in a table: comparison of solution types. Cost

reszek.cim: What is worth comparing — without a specific price
reszek.szoveg: What is worth comparing — without a specific price A final price cannot responsibly be given without a survey. The categories below, however, can be compared across all the directions. 01 Investment. Alongside the price of the unit, the earthworks, the depth of the connection and the disposal of the treated water — the latter are often the larger items. 02 Energy. Continuous with an active system, absent with the other two. 03 Removal. With a sealed holding tank, regular emptying of the whole volume; with the other two, periodic sludge handling. 04 Maintenance and wearing parts. An active system has a compressor and membranes; a passive one has no moving parts. Outcome

reszek.cim: What you leave with should be a direction, not a product name
reszek.szoveg: What you leave with should be a direction, not a product name This page has served you if you leave it not with three product names but with a sense of which direction is worth pursuing. The final choice comes out of the plot and load data. 01 Towards active biological treatment. Typically for permanent occupation, where the load is predictable and where the drainage field either would not fit or is limited by the groundwater. Who does it suit? 02 Towards the septic tank. To be examined where the permeability of the soil is adequate, the groundwater sits deep enough, and there is enough free area for the drainage field. Who does it suit? 03 The sealed holding tank is a serious alternative. Where local conditions allow nothing at all to enter the ground. We do not manufacture this solution — but we will say so when it is the answer. 04 There is not yet enough data to choose. That too is a perfectly usable result. If the pattern of use, the load, the plot or the water disposal is uncertain, those are what to settle first — more product information is not what is missing. Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What people usually ask before deciding
reszek.szoveg: What people usually ask before deciding Does the treatment unit need electricity? That depends on the technology: an active biological system requires a continuous electricity supply, a sealed holding tank and a septic tank system do not. A precise consumption figure is only worth quoting from a documented or measured value — the per-model figures are in the unit's technical data sheet. Can it be done entirely without emptying? It is not worth starting from a „no emptying” promise that supposedly holds for every system. Emptying a sealed holding tank is a fundamental part of how it works; with the septic tank and the active system, periodic sludge handling remains. These are two different operating questions and have to be examined separately. Can the system smell? The question of odour is not worth closing with a single general promise. Proper design, use and operation all count together; and where behaviour is abnormal the cause has to be found, not the symptom masked. Which needs less maintenance? Passive systems have no moving or electrical parts; in an active system the compressor and membrane are wearing parts. That does not settle it on its own, however: the owner's duties and the servicing needed together give the picture, and it is worth comparing that from the data of the specific unit. Next step

reszek.cim: Is a standalone system an option at all?
reszek.szoveg: Is a standalone system an option at all? Before you choose a technology, one question has to be settled: whether the mains sewer really is unavailable. That is not a question of the pipe in the street, nor a matter of opinion — official information decides it. Or look at what data the decision needs Mains sewer or a standalone system?

When is replacement warranted? The sealed holding tank is a lawful solution recognised in the regulations — it does not have to be replaced because it is bad technology. The reason for replacement always follows from your own situation, and keeping it is a legitimate outcome too. First, let us be clear

reszek.cim: The sealed holding tank is not faulty technology
reszek.szoveg: The sealed holding tank is not faulty technology The everyday word „cesspit” is not a technical term. The first thing to know is what is actually in the ground: a sealed, watertight holding tank, a septic tank system, or some older structure built on a different principle. The sealed holding tank is a lawful solution recognised in the regulations: its logic is collection and regular disposal. It does not have to be replaced because it is bad technology — but because, at that particular property, the use, the cost or the technical condition warrants it. So the reason for replacement always follows from your own situation, not from a general assertion. Reasons

reszek.cim: What argues for replacement, and what against
reszek.szoveg: What argues for replacement, and what against Replacement is indicated if… emptying is frequent, and arranging it is a burden in itself; the tank's capacity is inadequate for the way it is used now; odour, overflow or backing up appears; the household has grown or will grow; a refurbishment or garden works are planned anyway — part of the earthworks can then be shared; you are planning for the long term with the property. Keeping it or waiting is rational too, if… use is light, and emptying is infrequent; you only plan to use the property for a short time yet; construction of the mains sewer is scheduled, and the date is known; the system is sealed and sound, the emptying frequency has been steady for years; the problem can be narrowed to a single element — to the cover or the connecting pipe, for instance. What we cannot decide from here

reszek.cim: We do not diagnose structural condition with a questionnaire
reszek.szoveg: We do not diagnose structural condition with a questionnaire If the suspicion leakage, loss of watertightness or a structural fault, neither you nor we can judge that online. It takes an on-site investigation — and that is not a politeness but the limit of a responsible answer. You do not have to judge the tank's watertightness or structural condition. What you can gather: photographs, earlier documents, the emptying history and the symptoms observed. The rest is for the survey. Outcome

reszek.cim: Four kinds of conclusion — and none of them is „buy a unit”
reszek.szoveg: Four kinds of conclusion — and none of them is „buy a unit” 01 Worth examining further. The reasons are there; the next question is what system could take its place. 02 A technical survey is needed first. The symptoms point to a structural cause, which has to be looked at on site. 03 Costs have to be compared first. Replacement is not clear-cut economically — the total cost has to be looked at, not the emptying charge. 04 Replacement is not clearly warranted at present. That is a valid result too, and we will say so when it is the case. Next step

reszek.cim: If replacement is warranted: what can take its place?
reszek.szoveg: If replacement is warranted: what can take its place? There is a choice between three operating models, and what decides between them is not price but the use, the plot and the operating duty you can take on. Or look at the total cost Cesspit, septic tank or biological?
Documents and certificates Every technical claim has to lead to a document. That is the difference between a marketing claim and usable technical information. What this page will be

reszek.cim: A single, versioned body of evidence
reszek.szoveg: A single, versioned body of evidence The aim is for this page to be the single authoritative, up-to-date home for the A.B.Clear products' technical and conformity papers — searchable by model and document type. Today this body of evidence is scattered: the CE and EN 12566-3 conformity, the accredited testing, the patent and the earlier permit examples all appear separately on the site, but they do not add up to a versioned document library. This is one of the largest untapped opportunities for A.B.Clear's technical credibility — and, frankly, the easiest to put right. Which documents belong here

reszek.cim: The structure of the document library
reszek.szoveg: The structure of the document library Every paper has to carry: model, version, date of issue, validity status and document owner. 01 Declaration of performance and CE document. Per model, indicating the link to EN 12566-3. 02 Test report. The full accredited test document the outlet water values refer to. 03 Operating and maintenance manual. Per model, with the current version. 04 Installation guide. For the contractor and the client alike. 05 Technical data sheet and product drawing. Dimensions, levels, connections. 06 Warranty and guarantee. Together with the terms. 07 Szabadalmi document. For the sludge bag solution, with status by country. 08 Examples of earlier permits. Marked strictly as „example, historical document” — these do NOT prove that a permit would be granted automatically today. Why versioning matters

Two separate needs New sales The current models need their current documents The conformity reference has to point at the standard in force The designer needs today's data sheet, not last year's A valid document is needed for the regulatory procedure Supporting older products A unit installed ten years ago belongs with the manual OF THAT TIME Supplying parts requires knowing the production version The old document has to stay available — with archive status The two must not be confused: anyone operating an old system should not be given today's data sheet The chain of evidence

Claim → document → source Every technical claim has to lead to a document, and every document has to be identifiable. If we write that the unit conforms to a standard, the conformity paper should be one click away. This is not a formality. For the designer, the contractor and the regulator, this is precisely the difference between a marketing claim and usable technical information — and it is what competitors typically do not do. In the meantime

Ask for what you need Until the document library is assembled, we send the papers you need directly. Write and tell us which model and which document — and what you need it for, because that decides which version is the right one. Technical data Get in touch Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Can I have the declaration of performance before buying? Yes. Write and tell us which model interests you and we will send it. For design and for a permitting procedure it is often necessary anyway. Where do I find documentation for my older unit? Give us the type of unit and roughly the year of installation — we will find the documentation belonging to it from that time. Today's data sheet is not necessarily valid for a system installed ten years ago. Do the earlier permit examples prove that it will be permitted? No. Those are 2020 documents belonging to particular projects, and they do not mean a permit would be granted automatically today. They are useful as examples — they show what data such a procedure contained — but today's rules always have to be checked from a current source.
Installation requirements These are not details but preconditions of the works. What we settle in advance costs nothing extra at the edge of the pit. Why it has its own page

reszek.cim: It should not emerge from the small print
reszek.szoveg: It should not emerge from the small print The installation preconditions have until now been scattered: some among the FAQs, some in the small print of the order form. This page gathers them in one place — because they are not details but preconditions of the works. The aim is that the project should not begin with surprises on site. What we settle here in advance costs nothing extra at the edge of the pit. Preparing the site

What has to be provided? 01 The position of the tank. At an adequate distance from the building, the well and the plot boundary, planned together with access for servicing. 02 The level of the inlet pipe. This determines whether a riser element or a pumping chamber is needed. The exact per-model values need to be confirmed — see the note below. 03 Groundwater and anchoring the tank. In high groundwater a concrete surround or another anchored arrangement is needed against flotation. 04 The path of the treated water. The position and design of the soakaway or other disposal arrangement — a precondition of the project, not a later addition. 05 Electrical supply point. A properly protected electrical connection to the unit. 06 Vehicle loading. Vehicles cannot be driven over the tank without a separately sized concrete chamber. 07 Access for machinery. Access width, overhanging obstructions, the route for lowering it in, where the spoil goes. 08 Access for servicing. The cover has to remain openable and accessible for good. Who carries it out

Division of responsibility This may be the client or their own contractor Earthworks, excavating the pit Laying the pipework from the house Building the electrical supply point Building the disposal arrangement for the treated water Backfill and reinstating the ground Delivery — can also be arranged yourself Available as an ÖkoTech service Delivery to site Installation Commissioning and start-up Handover and training the owner These are separate service items, not automatically part of ordering the unit Handover and training

reszek.cim: What happens at the end of the works
reszek.szoveg: What happens at the end of the works Commissioning is not switching the unit on. It includes checking that the system works, setting the controller and — what is most often left out — the owner's training. The training covers how to carry out the settlement test, how to handle the sludge bag, what the controller's indications mean and what has to be checked routinely. It is worth taking seriously — the system's long-term operation turns on it. The handover is documented, and the papers belonging to the unit — operating manual, declaration of performance, guarantee — pass over at that point. Next step

The plot data comes first Most of the installation requirements are plot data. Once you have it, the works can be planned — if not, an on-site survey closes the open questions. Documents and certificates Plot suitability Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Can it be installed by my own contractor? The earthworks, pipework and electrical supply point can typically be carried out by your own contractor. Installation and commissioning are separate service items — we agree their terms with the specific order, because the guarantee can be tied to them. How long does the installation take? That depends on the earthworks and the conditions on site. Placing the unit is a short process in itself; the whole works — including building the disposal arrangement — typically takes several days. We can give an exact schedule on the specific project. Is a permit required? That depends on the project and the location, and the procedural rules change from time to time. Our earlier permit examples are from 2020 and cannot be used as today's procedural rules. The project preparation section deals with this, citing current sources.
Models and capacities Transparency about capacity — but not automatic model selection. The actual consumption, the peak load and the plot data are all part of the decision too. What this page is for

Transparency about capacity This page sets out the whole range in a single consistent data structure so that a designer and a contractor can work from it: nominal population equivalent, hydraulic capacity, range of application, tank size and every technical parameter that genuinely affects the choice of model. What it does not give: automatic model selection. Transparency about capacity is not the same as a visitor picking the right unit alone, from a single figure. What data is needed

reszek.cim: These are needed for each model
reszek.szoveg: These are needed for each model This list is also the list of missing data — see the note below. 01 Nominal population equivalent (PE). The organic load capacity. 02 Maximum daily hydraulic capacity (m³/day). This is always needed alongside „persons”. 03 Inlet and outlet levels. These determine what pipe depth it can be installed at without a riser. 04 Dimensions and weight. For planning the excavation and the lift into place. 05 Nominal and peak load capability. Only with verified, documented figures — see below. 06 Underload range. How far below the nominal it runs stably. 07 Version and date. Which production variant the figure applies to. On the overload figures

reszek.cim: Why they do not appear in the table
reszek.szoveg: Why they do not appear in the table Our current material contains two different overload claims: one says the unit withstands a sustained 30% overload, the other that for 2–3 days it can handle as much as 150%. Both claims may well be true at once — they speak of different timescales. They can go into a capacity table only once it is documented what the percentage refers to (headcount, volume of water or organic load), which models, for how long, at what temperature and against what outlet water quality criterion. Without these the percentage is too easily misread — and in sizing it is exactly this kind of figure that causes trouble later. So we would rather publish no number than one we cannot qualify. When it leaves the standard band

Two boundaries Standard model selection Wastewater domestic in character The load falls within the nominal range The peaks are predictable and regular The plot conditions are known A catalogue model and the usual arrangement Bespoke engineering route A load above 50 PE Non-domestic or process wastewater A highly unpredictable load profile A solution for several properties or part of a settlement Bespoke design, a different permitting route Next step

The profile is the input Choosing a model is not the first step but the result of the load profile. Once that is known, the question of the model is clearer — and there is no need to size for the maximum. Technical data Load profile and capacity pre-qualifier Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Why there is no capacity table here? Because our public material currently has no consistent data sheet covering every model. We would rather say what is missing than publish incomplete or contradictory figures. On a specific project our engineering colleagues give exact figures. Should we size for the maximum number of guests? No. A larger system chosen for a peak that occurs a few times a year would be persistently underloaded on every other day — and that is an operating problem in its own right. The average and the regular peak together are the right starting point.

reszek.cim: Why we do not argue with this
reszek.szoveg: Why we do not argue with this Our site mentions a total number of installations in several places, and the figures are not consistent — they come from content produced at different times. So we do not make a market-leadership claim of the „most installations in Hungary” kind here. Without a current, dated figure and a basis for comparison such a claim cannot be verified — and what cannot be verified is not evidence. We argue with projects instead. Sludge bag technology ÖkoTech's strongest product-specific difference. Not a „maintenance-free” solution — a different model of sludge handling, with clear conditions. The problem

reszek.cim: Why does sludge have to be handled at all?
reszek.szoveg: Why does sludge have to be handled at all? During active biological treatment surplus sludge is produced — the bacteria multiply and the surplus has to be drawn off. If that does not happen the system silts up and the treatment efficiency falls. The conventional solution is regular emptying: a tanker comes from time to time and takes the accumulated sludge away. That works, but it is a recurring cost and something to arrange — and precisely what many people choose a system to avoid. At large treatment plants, however, it does not work that way: there, managing the sludge level is a continuous, even process. ÖkoTech's own development carried that logic across to household scale. How it works

The sludge bag solution 01 Sludge thickening chamber. The surplus sludge passes into a separate chamber where it thickens — most of its water content separates out again. 02 Water return. The water that separates out returns to the process. So it is not water that leaves; what remains is the actual quantity of sludge. 03 The sludge bag. The thickened sludge passes into a bag where it dewaters further. The bag retains the solids. 04 Handling the bag. When it is full, it has to be dealt with. This is the owner's task, and it is part of the process — not an exception but the point of the model. „Zero emptying” means precisely

reszek.cim: What it means, and what it does not
reszek.szoveg: What it means, and what it does not The sludge bag solution under normal operating conditions it does away with regular emptying. That is a real, documentable advantage, and a significant difference from the conventional solutions. What it does not mean: that there is nothing to do about the sludge. Checking and adjusting the sludge level is a genuine operating task, and handling the bag is the owner's too. So the sludge bag is not a „maintenance-free” solution but a different model of sludge handling. There can also be exceptional situations — a malfunction, sustained overload, damage to the biology — where other intervention is needed after all. Better to know that in advance than to be disappointed later. Put this way the advantage is not weakened. On the contrary: it becomes verifiable, and it raises no expectation that reality cannot meet. Two models of sludge handling

How it works If you understand one concept — activated sludge — everything else follows: aeration, chemical sensitivity, the load limits and sludge handling alike. The process

What happens to the wastewater? The path of the wastewater from the house, inlet to outlet. The exact number of chambers and their arrangement differ from model to model. 01 Inlet and mechanical pre-treatment. The wastewater arrives by gravity. In the first chamber the coarser solids settle and the breakdown begins. 02 Aerated chamber — this is where the treatment happens. A membrane blower introduces fine bubbles into the water. Supplied with oxygen, the bacteria — the activated sludge — break down the organic matter. 03 Settlement. After aeration the water comes to rest and the sludge settles. Clear water is left on top, the denser sludge layer below. 04 Sludge return. Part of the settled sludge returns to the aerated chamber: this is what sustains the bacterial community. 05 Surplus sludge removal. The bacteria multiply, so a surplus is produced continuously. Unless it is drawn off, the system silts up. Handling this is one of the A.B.Clear's distinguishing features. 06 Treated water outlet. The treated water leaves the unit — and from here the question of water disposal follows, which is a subject in itself. Activated sludge

What everything else follows from „Activated sludge” is not dirt but a living mass of bacteria — this is what does the cleaning. Understand that one concept and everything else follows. Why is aerationneeded? Because these bacteria work with oxygen. Why is the system sensitive to chemicals ? Because disinfectant kills them. Why is sustained underloadinga problem? Because they starve. Why is overloading? Because they cannot keep up. And why is sludge handling? Because they multiply, and the excess has to be drawn off. The condition of the activated sludge is therefore not a technical curiosity but the measure of the system's health — that is what the settlement (sludge) test measures, and it has to be carried out regularly as part of operation.
