reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often How often does it have to be emptied? We give no figure for this at present, because two of our own sources word it differently, and this has to be reconciled from the manufacturer's guidance and real operating data. What is certain: the sludge level governs, not the calendar, and the frequency is determined by the size of the tank and the intensity of use. What does emptying cost? We publish no specific amount: emptying charges differ from place to place and over time. What can be planned on: that it is a recurring operating cost, and that at less frequently used properties it arises considerably less often. Is a bacterial additive really needed? Our current material recommends regular dosing, with a repeat refresher after a longer break. The manufacturer's guidance belonging to the unit records this exactly — ask for it for the specific product. What should I do if I notice an odour? Check the ventilation and the filter first. If the smell persists, or there is damp over the field as well, that can point to saturation — it is then worth having a specialist look at it before the field is lastingly damaged.
How it works The process has two stages. Anaerobic pre-treatment takes place in the tank, but the substance of the treatment happens in the ground, in the drainage field. The process

reszek.cim: The path of the wastewater, step by step
reszek.szoveg: The path of the wastewater, step by step 01 Entry into the septic tank. The household wastewater arrives in the tank by gravity. 02 Settlement and scum layer. The heavier solids sink to the bottom, the lighter matter — fats and oils — forms a scum layer on the surface. The relatively clearer liquid phase remains between the two. 03 Anaerobic breakdown. In the oxygen-poor environment, bacteria break down the organic matter. This is a slower process than the aerobic one, and it does not complete the treatment either. 04 Filtration. On the outlet side a filter retains solids that would otherwise pass on. This protects the drainage field from clogging — which is why it has to be checked regularly. 05 A drainage field. The pre-treated water reaches the ground evenly through a distribution system. This is where the system's second treatment stage takes place. 06 Aerobic treatment in the soil. Micro-organisms living in the upper, aerated layer of the field break the organic matter down further. This needs oxygen — which is why it is critical that the layer does not become compacted. 07 Disposal into the soil. The treated water percolates into the deeper layers. Why the tank is not enough

The most common misunderstanding The septic tank on its own pre-treats: it settles and breaks down anaerobically. The treatment substance of it, however, happens in the drainage field, in the upper aerated layer of the soil — where oxygen is available. So the field cannot be left out, made smaller, or put off on a „we shall do it later” basis. Without a drainage field this is not a septic tank system but a sealed tank that sooner or later fills up. Nor, for the same reason, can the field simply be moved: its position, size and design are part of the technology, not a question of layout. What it needs, and what it does not

The conditions for operation It does not need Electricity Kompresszor, aeration Control, automatika A continuous load to sustain the biology Regular electricity consumption What it needs Gravity or an engineered means of conveying the water Adequate ventilation A properly SIZED drainage field Suitable soil and favourable groundwater conditions Sufficient free area Periodic emptying and a bacterial additive Next step

reszek.cim: Does this suit the way you use the property?
reszek.szoveg: Does this suit the way you use the property? Once you understand how it works comes the question of whether your own pattern of use fits it — and whether the plot will take the drainage field. Drainage field and space required Who does it suit? Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Why does it need emptying if the bacteria break it down? Because anaerobic breakdown does not make the solids disappear; it only partly breaks them down. What remains — the non-degradable part and the by-products of decomposition — accumulates at the bottom. This has to be removed from time to time, or it narrows the tank and burdens the filter too. What happens in winter? The process slows but does not stop. The tank sits in the ground, which is favourable for temperature. It is precisely the winter period of low load that this technology takes well — which is why it is relevant at seasonal properties. How long does such a system last? The tank is long-lived, but the life of the drainage field depends on the load, the soil and the maintenance. Renewing a clogged or saturated field is substantial work — which is why correct sizing and protecting the area over the field matter.

Septic tank system Not simply a tank put in the ground: a system of septic tank and drainage field that works without electricity. A substantial part of the treatment happens in the ground. The first thing to settle

Not a tank — a system A septic tank system is not simply a tank put in the ground. Under the regulations in force a water facility consisting of a septic tank and a drainage fieldthat breaks down the pollutants and disposes of the wastewater on site without any energy input. The process has two stages. In the in the septic tank settlement and anaerobic — oxygen-free — pre-treatment take place. The pre-treated water then passes to the into the drainage field , where aerobic treatment continues in the ground. So the treatment does not finish in the tank. We put it this way because our earlier material said in one place that a septic tank „only stores and settles” the wastewater. That is partly true of the tank itself, but as a description of the whole system it is inaccurate — and it leaves out precisely the point. Two stages

What happens where Septic tank — first stage The heavier solids settle to the bottom The lighter matter floats up and forms a scum layer Anaerobic breakdown begins in the oxygen-poor environment The water passes on through a filter The sludge accumulates here — which is why it has to be emptied from time to time It requires no electricity Drainage field — second stage The pre-treated water reaches the ground through a distribution system An aerobic process takes place in the upper, aerated layer of the soil A substantial part of the treatment happens HERE So the field is not drainage but a technological element It typically needs more area than a soakaway Its size depends on the soil and the load The main advantage — and its condition

Operation without electricity The most important advantage of the technology is that requires no electricity. There is no compressor, no aeration, no controller — and no living bacterial culture that has to be kept alive by a continuous load. This is particularly relevant for holiday homes, weekend houses and hunting lodges used with long gaps. Where an active system's long winter break would call for a separate procedure, this technology is more forgiving. It does not follow, however, that „holiday home = septic tank”. For the drainage field to work properly it also takes sufficient area, suitable soil, favourable groundwater conditions and proper sizing. Government Decree 147/2010 itself ties the sizing of the facility to taking these into account. The pages in this section

A regular feladatok Needing no electricity does not mean having nothing to do. These are worth thinking through in advance. 01 Periodic emptying. The bottom sludge and the scum layer accumulating in the tank have to be removed. On the frequency see the note below — our figures are currently contradictory, so we publish no number. 02 Bacterial additive. Our current material recommends a regular bacterial refresher, with a repeat dose after a longer break. This is a genuine recurring task and a consumables cost — a substantial difference from an active system, where the culture is self-sustaining. 03 Checking the filter. The filter at the septic tank outlet can clog; its condition has to be checked. 04 Watching the drainage field. Odour, damp at the surface or backing up can all be signs that the field is becoming saturated. 05 Documentation. The regulations also require documents relating to the lawful disposal of the waste produced to be retained — it is worth keeping the emptying receipts. Next step

How it works comes first Once you understand the two stages, the other questions — the area required, the emptying, the bacterial additive — follow of themselves. Then comes whether it suits the way you use the property. The EPURECO range How it works Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is this the same as a cesspit? No. A cesspit is typically an unsealed tank without a drainage field, and often leaking. A septic tank system is a permittable water facility consisting of a sealed tank and a properly sized drainage field, in which actual treatment takes place. Does it really need no electricity? It does not. That is one of the technology's main advantages. In exchange it needs more area, asks for regular emptying and a bacterial additive, and the quality of the outlet water is harder to document than with an active system. How much area does it need? We give no single figure for this, because the size of the field depends on the measured infiltration capacity of the soil, the daily load and the groundwater. The same household needs a much smaller area on one soil and several times that on another — which is why measurement is required. Is this always the right choice for a holiday home? This is often the more relevant direction, but not automatically. The area the drainage field needs, the soil and the groundwater are conditions just as much — and there are holiday homes where those are exactly why it cannot be built. Does it smell? In normal operation and with adequate ventilation it is not typical. Odour is a signal: a filling tank, a blocked filter or a saturating drainage field can all cause it — a check is then needed.

When it is not suitable Needing no electricity, and simplicity, do not on their own make it right for every property. And some things are not technical exclusions but a question of what you can live with.

reszek.cim: Needing no electricity is not the answer to everything
reszek.szoveg: Needing no electricity is not the answer to everything A septic tank system is simple and needs no electricity. That does not make it right for every property without a mains sewer — and the commonest constraint is not the tank but the drainage field. This page keeps apart what is an exclusion, and what is suitable subject to further examination can be. The two are not the same, and neither are their consequences. Two degrees of severity

Exclusion and conditional suitability Typically an exclusion There is not enough area for a drainage field of the required size The soil's infiltration capacity is inadequate and cannot be improved The legal applicability of a standalone system is not established in that place Non-domestic wastewater of process origin, without investigation A significant commercial kitchen or industrial load, without pre-treatment It may be suitable subject to separate examination High groundwater — the position of the field can be changed Cohesive soil — a larger field or a different arrangement A smaller plot — the layout decides, not the square metres A well nearby — the field can be moved Permanent occupation — a larger field, more frequent emptying In these cases measurement and an expert opinion settle the question What is not a technical exclusion

reszek.cim: The question of what you can live with
reszek.szoveg: The question of what you can live with Sometimes the system is technically feasible but the owner will not take on what comes with it. That is a perfectly legitimate decision — only it is not a technical exclusion but an objection about use, and so a category of its own. This covers regular emptying arranging the emptying and its cost, along with bacterial additive dosing regularly. Neither is a large task, but both recur, and if someone does not want them from the outset, the system will not work well. It is then worth looking at what the active biological system gives in exchange: no regular emptying and no dosing, but it needs electricity and regular checks. The result

Four possible outcomes 01 It does not javasolt. On the circumstances known, the technology is unsuitable — typically because of the area the drainage field needs, or the soil. 02 A plot investigation is needed. The question is not the technology but the plot's characteristics. A percolation test and establishing the groundwater follow. 03 A biological system should be examined. Because of the usage profile or the lack of space, the active system may be the better option — the two are worth looking at side by side. 04 A different solution is needed. If neither on-site disposal nor the biological system is in play, the sealed holding tank or another direction remains. Next step

reszek.cim: Look at the other direction too
reszek.szoveg: Look at the other direction too If you are unsure because of the lack of space or because of permanent occupation, it is worth looking at the two technologies side by side against the same criteria. Biological wastewater treatment Comparing solution types Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is it ruled out on a small plot? Not automatically, but this is the commonest constraint. The area a drainage field needs is typically larger than that of an active system's soakaway — so on a small plot the active system is often what remains realistic. The decision needs measurement, not estimation. Agyagos talajon works? With more difficulty, with a larger field, and in some places not at all. A percolation test decides it. If the soil will not take the daily volume of water, changing technology does not help on its own — because an active system's soakaway has to take the water too. I do not want to deal with emptying. That is a valid consideration and nothing to be embarrassed about. It is then worth looking at the active biological system: there is no regular emptying there, but it needs electricity and regular checks. The two systems place different burdens on the owner.

Who does it suit? Operating without electricity is a real advantage where the gaps are long. But suitability is not decided by property type — there are four conditions, and all four have to be met. The primary case

An intermittently used property The technology's primary field of application is a property not in continuous use: a holiday home, weekend house, hunting lodge, weekend plot. In these situations operating without electricity is a real advantage. There is no electrical plant to keep running at a property empty for months, and no living bacterial culture for a long absence to wear down. The system simply waits. That is not an automatic rule, however. Suitability is decided not by property type but by four conditions — and all four have to be met. The four conditions

reszek.cim: What has to be checked beyond the property type
reszek.szoveg: What has to be checked beyond the property type 01 Domestic-type wastewater. Kitchen, bathroom, WC. With a significant kitchen, process or industrial load the system cannot be sized from headcount alone. 02 Suitable soil. For the drainage field to work the soil has to take the water. This has to be measured — the name of the soil is not enough of a figure. 03 Favourable groundwater conditions. The field has to work above the groundwater, in an aerated layer. In high groundwater this can be a constraint. 04 Sufficient area. The area the drainage field needs is the largest real constraint — larger than the soakaway of an active system. It has to fit in what remains after the house, the well, the driveway and any planned structures. Typical situations

reszek.cim: Where it is a good choice, and where it needs examination
reszek.szoveg: Where it is a good choice, and where it needs examination Typically a good choice A holiday home used only in summer A weekend house with longer breaks A hunting lodge in seasonal use A property where there is no power supply, or it is unreliable A large plot where the drainage field fits Well-draining soil, low groundwater This needs separate examination A permanently occupied family home A small or heavily built-up plot Cohesive, clayey soil High, or seasonally high, groundwater A well nearby, water base protection status A commercial kitchen or non-domestic load For permanent occupation

reszek.cim: Why we recommend the active system instead
reszek.szoveg: Why we recommend the active system instead For a permanently occupied family home we typically recommend the active biological system. There the continuous load is exactly what that technology is for, the outlet water quality is measurably better, and it takes less space. This does not mean a septic tank system is ruled out for permanent occupation — rather that there, the larger drainage field and the regular emptying are a price that buys less than it does at a seasonal property. If it is the direction after all — because there is no electricity, for instance — the plot's characteristics have to be examined especially carefully, because permanent use means a greater load and a larger field. Next step

The plot decides The substance of suitability turns on the drainage field: whether the area required will fit, and whether the soil will take the daily volume of water. When it is not suitable Drainage field and space required Frequently asked questions

reszek.cim: What we are asked most often
reszek.szoveg: What we are asked most often Is this the best solution for a holiday home? Often the more relevant direction, particularly with a long winter gap or where there is no electricity. But not automatically: the area the drainage field needs, the soil and the groundwater are conditions just as much. There are holiday homes where those are exactly why it cannot be built. Is it right for a family home too? For permanent occupation we typically recommend the active biological system — better outlet water quality, less space. A septic tank system comes into play there mainly where there is no power supply or it is unreliable, and the plot will take the larger field. What if we do not use it for years? The system takes a long break — that is one of its main advantages. After a longer gap, dosing a bacterial additive is recommended to restart it. The unit's documentation records the exact procedure. Does it need emptying at a holiday home too? Yes, only less often, because the load is smaller. The frequency depends on the size of the tank, the occupancy and the intensity of use — which is why we publish no fixed interval.

reszek.cim: Four levels, and each of them can change the direction

Whether there is continuous power, whether emptying is acceptable, what maintenance the owner will take on. What it does ad

Which solution suits which case? Knowing the technological differences, the next question is how they apply to your own situation. This page starts from situations rather than products — and in some cases the answer is that data has to be gathered first. How to read this

reszek.cim: A direction to examine, not a product recommendation
reszek.szoveg: A direction to examine, not a product recommendation The situations below are not product assignments. Each says which direction is worth examining first, and what can override it. There are situations too where the next task is not choosing a technology but gathering data: checking the mains sewer, investigating the groundwater or obtaining laboratory results. Situations

reszek.cim: Nine typical situations, and what is worth looking at first in each
reszek.szoveg: Nine typical situations, and what is worth looking at first in each A permanently occupied family home Examining an active biological system A steady, continuous load is the operating condition biological treatment is built on. The plot's characteristics and the disposal of the treated water can override it, however. What can change it: no continuous power · the treated water cannot be disposed of · the plot cannot be reached by machine Holiday home, weekend house, a long seasonal break Examining the septic tank direction Long stretches with no load are hard on the biological community. The process in the ground is less sensitive to a break — where the drainage field has enough room and the soil allows it. What can change it: cohesive soil · high groundwater · not enough area for the drainage field Replacing an existing cesspit Assess the existing system first A replacement does not begin with choosing a technology. The condition and depth of the old structure and the route of the connecting pipe determine what can be installed in its place and with what earthworks. What can change it: decommissioning the old system is a permitting question too A small plot, or one that drains poorly An active biological system or a sealed holding tank The area the drainage field needs is the bottleneck here. With no room for it, the septic tank direction drops out — not from technical preference but from geometry. What can change it: if the treated water cannot be disposed of either, the sealed holding tank remains High or widely fluctuating groundwater A groundwater investigation first, technology only after The design groundwater level bears on both the installation and the water disposal. It is not necessarily disqualifying, but it may call for a separate technical arrangement.

reszek.cim: Nine typical situations, and what is worth looking at first in each (part 2)
reszek.szoveg: What can change it: the decision needs measurement, not estimation There is no electricity on the plot The septic tank direction or a sealed holding tank An active biological system requires a continuous power supply. Without electricity this direction drops out, whatever the other conditions. What can change it: a temporary power supply is not enough for continuous operation Guesthouse, restaurant, institution, campsite A sized system, not a domestic unit Here the peak load and the composition of the wastewater decide, not the headcount on its own. The technology comes after the sizing. What can change it: kitchen wastewater needs pre-treatment as well Non-domestic, industrial or process wastewater Laboratory analysis, the expert route Biological treatment is for domestic wastewater. Where the composition differs, the standard quotation route breaks off and examination decides. What can change it: this is not a question that can be settled online The mains sewer is expected within a foreseeable time Check the development schedule first If the connection is scheduled and the date known, a parallel investment is hard to justify. A promise and a schedule, however, are not the same thing. What can change it: ask the local authority for a binding date Next step

Településszintű szennyvízkezelésnél a megoldás nem a berendezésen múlik elsősorban, hanem azon, hogy ingatlanonkénti vagy központi kialakítás illik-e a település szerkezetéhez, és mit enged a helyi szabályozás. Ezt felmérés nélkül nem lehet megmondani — de az első beszélgetés elköteleződés nélkül zajlik. Vagy nézze meg a nagyobb és közösségi rendszereket Kapcsolatfelvétel Gyakori kérdések

reszek.lap: Bakonypéterd — központi telep, amelyet ma a közműszolgáltató üzemeltet
reszek.szoveg: Amit a leggyakrabban kérdeznek Meddig tart egy ilyen projekt? A településméret és a kialakítás dönti el. Az ingatlanonkénti telepítés ütemezhető, a központi telep egy összefüggő beruházás. A reális ütemtervet a felmérés és az engedélyezési feltételek ismeretében tudjuk megadni. Ki üzemelteti a rendszert az átadás után? Ingatlanonkénti kialakításnál a tulajdonos, a mi szervizhátterünkkel. Központi telepnél az üzemeltető lehet az önkormányzat vagy a területi közműszolgáltató — Bakonypéterden például a Pannon-Víz Zrt. vette át. Van pályázati lehetőség ilyen projektre? Volt és lehet — a csikvándi projekt a Vidékfejlesztési Program keretében valósult meg. A mindenkori kiírásokat az önkormányzatnál és a pályázati portálokon érdemes követni; a műszaki tartalom összeállításában tudunk segíteni.

Clear berendezést telepítettünk és üzemeltünk be, házanként. Ez volt Magyarországon az elsőként lezárt, elkészült szennyvíztisztítási projekt a Vidékfejlesztési Program pályázati keretében. Háttér

reszek.lap: Csikvánd — 128 egyedi berendezés egy egész faluban
reszek.szoveg: Miért így oldottuk meg 01 Nem volt közcsatorna, és nem is épült. A településen a hálózat kiépítése nem volt reális, ezért a szennyvízkezelést ingatlanonként kellett megoldani. 02 Százhuszonnyolc külön telek, százhuszonnyolc külön adottság. Minden ingatlanon külön kellett megnézni a csőkivezetés mélységét, a talajt és a kezelt víz elhelyezését — ez a projekt legnagyobb szervezési feladata. 03 Pályázati keret, kötött határidővel. A Vidékfejlesztési Program elszámolási rendje pontos ütemezést kívánt; a projekt az országban elsőként zárult le. Hasonló helyzet

A projekt egy lapon Helyszín Óbudavár, Balaton-felvidék Kivitelezés éve 2011 Keret minisztériumi mintaprojekt Megoldás településszintű szennyvízkezelés Alvállalkozó kizárólag a négy monitoringkút létesítéséhez A feladat

A minisztériumi keret együtt járt a monitorozással: négy monitoringkút létesült a hatás követésére. 02 Ez volt az első településszintű munkánk. Amit itt tanultunk a szervezésről és a telepítésről, az minden későbbi projektben visszaköszön. 03 Tizenöt év távlatából is működik. A polgármester visszajelzése nem az átadáskor született, hanem évekkel később. Visszajelzés
